introVerses.text: And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth.
Their meat will not reach Allah, nor will their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you.
Say, 'Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it.'
And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.
And [saying], 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him.'
O you who believe! Turn to Allah with sincere repentance.
O you who believe! Endure and be more patient.
We shall test you with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits... glad tidings to the patient.
O you who believe! Fear Allah and be with the truthful.
...the truthful men and the truthful women...for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward.
Had they been truthful to Allah, it would have been much better for them.
Who sees you when you stand up (in prayer) and sees your movements with those who prostrate.
He is with you wherever you are.
Nothing is hidden from Allah in the heavens or in the earth.
Surely your Sustainer is Ever-watchful.
He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the hearts conceal.
O you who believe! Fear Allāh as He should be feared.
So fear Allāh as best you can.
O you who believe! Fear Allāh and speak what is right.
Whoever fears Allāh, He makes a way out for him and provides for him from sources he would never have imagined.
O believers! If you continually fear Allāh, He shall grant you a criterion (to judge between right and wrong), and expiate your sins, and forgive you. And Allāh is of great bounty.

7.title: Chapter 7: Conviction and Reliance on Allah

introVerses.text: When the believers saw the confederates, they said: 'This is what Allāh and His Messenger had promised us and Allāh and His Messenger had spoken the truth. This only increased their conviction and submission (to Allāh and His Messenger).'

Those to whom the people said: 'The people have gathered against you, so fear them!' This only increased their faith and they said: 'Allāh is sufficient for us and He is the best of helpers.' So they returned with Allāh's grace and bounty, without any harm even touching them.
Place your trust in the Ever-living who cannot die.
And only in Allāh should the believers place their trust.
Once you have made a decision, place your trust in Allāh.
And whoever places his trust in Allāh, He is sufficient for him.
The believers are those whose hearts tremble when the name of Allāh is mentioned, whose faith increases when His words are recited to them and who place their trust only in their Sustainer.
So remain steadfast, as you have been ordered.

Surely those who said: 'Our Sustainer is Allāh' and then remain steadfast, angels descend upon them, saying: 'Do not fear and do not grieve; and rejoice with the glad tidings of Paradise which you have been promised. We are your friends in this world as well as in the Hereafter. There you shall have whatever your heart desires and you shall have whatever you ask for. This is hospitality from the Most-Forgiving, the Most-Merciful.'

Surely those who say: 'Our Sustainer is Allāh', and are then steadfast, they will have no fear nor shall they grieve. They are the people of Paradise, where they will live forever, as a reward for what that they used to do.
I give you only one advice: that you stand up for Allāh's sake in pairs and individually and then reflect.

Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth and in the alternation of night and day are signs for those who have intelligence. They remember Allāh standing, sitting and lying down and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth. They say: 'O our Sustainer! You have not created this in vain. We proclaim Your purity from all defects.'

Do they not look at the camels and see how they are created? And at the sky, how it is raised? And at the mountains, how they are firmly placed? And at the earth, how it is spread out? So, (O Messenger of Allāh), keep on giving advice for you are only an advisor.
Have they not travelled in the land and seen...
So hasten towards good deeds.
Hasten towards the forgiveness of your Sustainer and towards Paradise, the width of which spans the heavens and the earth. It has been prepared for the Allāh-fearing.
As for those who strive in Our cause, We will certainly lead them to Our paths. Surely Allāh is with those who do good.
And worship your Sustainer until the certainty (death) comes to you.
And remember the name of your Sustainer and devote yourself to Him, in exclusive devotion.
And whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
Whatever good you send ahead for yourselves, you will find it with Allāh, much better in condition and more greater in reward.
And whatever good you spend, surely Allāh knows of it.

12.title: Chapter 12: Increasing Good Deeds in One's Latter Life

introVerses.text: Did We not grant you a sufficient age in your life so that lessons could have been learnt by those who wished to take lesson? (Sūrah Fāṭir, 37)

13.title: Chapter 13: Exposition of the Numerous Avenues of Doing Good

introVerses.text: And Allāh is well aware of the good you do.
Allāh is aware of whatever good you do.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good, will see it.
Whoever does good, does so for his own benefit.
Ṭāhā. We have not revealed to you the Qur'ān to cause you difficulty.
Allāh desires ease for you and does not desire hardship for you.

Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts submit to the remembrance of Allāh and to the truth that has been revealed? Do not be like those who were given the Book before, after which a long period of time elapsed and their hearts hardened.
Do not be like the woman who had shredded her yarn to pieces after spinning it firmly.
And worship your Sustainer until the certainty (death) comes to you.

16.title: Chapter 16: Upholding the Sunnah and Its Etiquettes

introVerses.text: Hold fast to what the Messenger gives you and refrain from what he forbids you.
He does not speak of his own desire. Whatever he says is revelation revealed to him.
Say: 'If you love Allāh, then follow me, Allāh will then love you and forgive your sins.'
There is an excellent example in the Messenger of Allāh for one who has hope in Allāh and the Last Day.
Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allāh.

17.title: Chapter 17: Obligation of Submitting to the Order of Allah

introVerses.text: By the oath of your Sustainer! They cannot be believers until they make you a judge in the disputes that arise among them and they do not find any dissatisfaction in their hearts for your decision and they accept with total submission.
When the believers are summoned to appear before Allāh and His Messenger so that he may pass judgment between them, all they say is: 'We hear and we obey.' These are the successful ones.

18.title: Chapter 18: Prohibition of Innovations in Religion

introVerses.text: After the truth, there is only deviation.
We have not omitted anything in the book.
Then if you dispute regarding any matter, then refer it to Allāh and the Messenger.
This is My straight path, so follow it. And do not follow other paths for they will deviate you from His path.
Say: 'If you love Allāh, then follow me, Allāh will then love you and forgive your sins.'

19.title: Chapter 19: Initiating a Good or Evil Way

introVerses.text: Those who say: 'O our Sustainer! Grant us from our wives and our children coolness of the eyes and make us leaders of the righteous.'
We made them leaders, who guided by Our command.

20.title: Chapter 20: Directing Towards Good and Inviting to Guidance or Misguidance

introVerses.text: Invite towards your Sustainer...
Invite to the path of your Sustainer with wisdom and good counsel.
Assist each other in good deeds and piety.
There should be a group from among you who invite towards good.

21.title: Chapter 21: Helping Each Other in Goodness and Fear of Allah

introVerses.text: Assist each other in good deeds and piety.
By the oath of time, surely man is at a loss; except those who believe, do good deeds, who encourage each other towards the truth and who encourage each other to exercise patience.
The believers are all brothers.
And I advise you.
And I am a trustworthy advisor to you.

23.title: Chapter 23: Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil

introVerses.text: There should be a group among you that invites towards good, commands what is good and forbids evil. These are the successful ones.
You are the best of all nations which has been raised for mankind. You command good and forbid evil.
Adopt forgiveness, command what is good and ignore the ignorant ones.
The believing men and believing women are supporters of each other. They command good and forbid evil.

Those who disbelieved from the Banī Isrā'īl were cursed on the tongues of Dāwūd and 'Īsā, the son of Maryam because they were disobedient and transgressed the bounds. They would not prevent each other from the evil, which they would commit. Evil indeed is that which they did!
Say: 'The truth is from your Sustainer. Whoever is willing should believe; and whoever is willing should disbelieve.'
Proclaim openly what you have been commanded.
We saved those who used to forbid evil and We seized those who did wrong with a dreadful punishment because of their disobedience.

24.title: Chapter 24: Severe Punishment for Contradicting One's Actions with One's Words

introVerses.text: Do you command the people to piety and forget yourselves, whereas you are the ones who recite the Book? Have you no understanding?
O you who believe! Why do you say that which you do not do? It is most abhorrent in the sight of Allāh that you say that which you do not do.
And I do not wish to oppose you, in a manner that I do the same thing that I forbid you from.

25.title: Chapter 25: The Command of Fulfilling Trusts

introVerses.text: Allāh commands you to return the trusts to their rightful owners.
We offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains but they refused to bear it and were afraid of it. Man bore it; he is very unjust and ignorant.

26.title: Chapter 26: Prohibition of Oppression and Command to Return Rights

introVerses.text: The oppressors will have no friend or intercessor who will be obeyed.
The unjust will have no helper.

27.title: Chapter 27: Honouring the Sanctity of Muslims

introVerses.text: Whoever respects that which Allāh has made sacred, then this will be best for him with his Sustainer.
Whoever respects the symbols of Allāh, then this is because of the piety of the hearts.
And lower your wings for the believers.

Whoever kills another for a reason other than in retaliation for another soul or spreading corruption on earth, then it is as if he has killed all of mankind. And whoever preserves a life, then it is as if he has preserved the lives of all of mankind.

28.title: Chapter 28: Concealing the Faults of Muslims

introVerses.text: For those who love to spread immorality to the believers, there shall be a painful punishment in this world and in the Hereafter.

29.title: Chapter 29: Fulfilling the Needs of Muslims

introVerses.text: And do good deeds so that you may be successful.
Whoever intercedes in a beautiful manner shall receive a share thereof.
There is no good in most of their deliberations except in him who commands charity, good deeds or reconciliation between people.
And reconciliation is best.
So fear Allāh and reconcile between yourselves.
The believers are all brothers. So reconcile between your brothers.

32.title: Chapter 32: Virtues of the Weak, Poor and Undistinguished Muslims

introVerses.text: Restrain yourself with those who invoke their Sustainer morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not divert your attention from them.

33.title: Chapter 33: Compassion for Orphans, Girls, the Weak, and the Destitute

introVerses.text: And lower your wings for the believers.

Restrain yourself with those who supplicate to their Sustainer morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. Do not divert your attention from them, with the intention of acquiring the adornment of this worldly life.
Do not be harsh on the orphan. Do not drive away the beggar.
Have you not seen the one who denies the Day of Judgment. He is the one who drives away the orphan and does not encourage feeding of the poor.
And live with them in kindness.

You will never be able to maintain perfect justice between wives however much you may desire to do so. However, do not ignore any of them totally, leaving her suspended. If you make peace and adopt taqwā, then surely Allāh is Most-Forgiving, Most-Merciful.

35.title: Chapter 35: Rights of a Husband over his Wife

introVerses.text: Men have charge of women because of the virtue Allāh gave to some of you over others and because of what they spend from their wealth. So the virtuous women are obedient and, in (the husband's) absence, protect that which Allāh has protected.

36.title: Chapter 36: Spending on One's Wife and Children

introVerses.text: And to whom the child is born (i.e. the father) upon him is the responsibility of feeding and clothing them in a good manner.

The wealthy person should spend according to his means. As for the one whose sustenance is constrained he should spend from that which Allāh has given him. Allāh does not burden a soul more than what He has given him.
Whatever you spend, He will replenish it.

37.title: Chapter 37: Spending from that which One Loves and that which is Superior in Quality

introVerses.text: You will never be able to acquire righteousness until you spend that which you love.
O you who believe! Spend of the pure things that you have earned and of that which We produce for you from the earth. Do not intend to spend inferior things.

38.title: Chapter 38: Obligation to Command One's Family to Obey Allah and Prohibit them from Disobeying Him

introVerses.text: Command your family to establish ṣalāh and you yourself remain steadfast upon it.
O you who believe! Save yourselves and your families from the fire...

39.title: Chapter 39: Rights of the Neighbour and Being Good to Him

introVerses.text: Worship Allāh, ascribe none as partners with Him and be kind to parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near neighbours, distant neighbours, the companion by your side, travellers and those in your possession.

40.title: Chapter 40: Kindness to Parents and Maintaining Ties of Kinship

introVerses.text: Worship Allāh and ascribe none as partners with Him and be kind to parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near neighbours, distant neighbours, a companion by your side, travellers and those in your possession.
Fear Allāh in whose name you ask of one another and be mindful of your relatives.
Those who join that which Allāh has commanded that it be joined.
We commanded man to be good to his parents.

Your Sustainer has commanded that you worship only Him and that you be kind to your parents. If any one of them or both of them reach old age in your lifetime, do not even say to them: 'Ooffl' and do not scold them. Speak to them with respect. Lower before them the wings of humility out of compassion and say: 'O Sustainer! Show mercy to them as they raised me when I was little.'
We gave man instructions regarding his parents. His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness and his weaning is within two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents.

41.title: Chapter 41: Prohibition of Disobeying Parents and Severing Ties of Kinship

introVerses.text: And perhaps if you are given authority, you will cause corruption on earth and sever family ties. These are the people whom Allāh cursed. So He made them deaf and blind.

Those who break the pledge of Allāh after confirming it, who sever that which Allāh commanded that it be joined and spread corruption on earth, for them shall be a curse and for them shall be an evil abode.

Your Sustainer has commanded that you worship only Him and that you be kind to your parents. If any one of them or both of them reach old age in your lifetime, do not even say to them: 'Ooffl' and do not scold them. Speak to them with respect. Lower before them the wings of humility out of compassion and say: 'O Sustainer! Show mercy to them as they raised me when I was little.'

42.title: Chapter 42: Virtues of Maintaining Good Relations with Friends of Parents, Relatives, Wife and All Those One is Encouraged to Honour

43.title: Chapter 43: Honouring the Family of the Messenger of Allah and an Exposition of their Virtues

introVerses.text: Allāh only wishes to rid you of filth, O family of the Messenger, and to purify you thoroughly.
Whoever honours the symbols of Allāh, then this is because of the piety of the hearts.

44.title: Chapter 44: Honouring Scholars, Elders and People of Goodness; Giving Preference to Them Over Others and Elevating their Status

introVerses.text: Say: 'Can those with knowledge be equal to those who do not have knowledge?' Only those who possess intelligence will ponder.

45.title: Chapter 45: Visiting the Righteous, Sitting with Them, Adopting Their Company, Loving Them, Requesting Their Prayers, and Visiting Blessed Places

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "When Mūsā said to his young servant: 'I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas even if I have to continue for many years.' When they reached the junction of the two seas, they forgot their fish and it tunnelled its way into the sea. When they proceeded further, Mūsā said to his young servant: 'Bring our food. Without doubt, we have experienced great fatigue on this journey.' He said: 'Did you not see that when we sought shelter by that rock, I forgot the fish? None but Shaiṭān made me forget to mention it. It made its way into the sea in a strange way.' He said: 'This is exactly what we were seeking.' So they retraced their steps. They then found a servant of Ours to whom We had granted mercy from Ourselves and to whom We had imparted Our knowledge. Mūsā said to him: 'Can I follow you on condition that you teach me some of the special knowledge that you have been taught?'" (Sūrah al-Kahf, 60-66)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Restrain yourself with those who call to their Sustainer morning and evening, seeking His pleasure." (Sūrah al-Kahf, 28)

46.title: Chapter 46: The Virtue of Loving Someone for the Sake of Allah, Encouraging It, and Informing the One You Love

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh. Those with him are stern against the unbelievers and compassionate amongst themselves. You will see them sometimes bowing and sometimes prostrating, seeking the bounty and pleasure of Allāh. Their hallmark is on their faces, because of the effect of prostration." (Sūrah al-Fatḥ, 29)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Those who, before them, had homes (in Madīnah Munawwarah) and had adopted the faith. They love those who migrate to them..." (Sūrah al-Ḥashr, 9)

47.title: Chapter 47: Signs of Allah's Love for a Person and Encouragement to Adopt These Qualities

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Say: 'If you love Allāh, then follow me so that Allāh may love you and forgive your sins. And Allāh is Most forgiving, Most merciful.'" (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 31)

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "O you who believe! Whoever among you turns away from his religion, then Allāh shall soon bring another nation whom He loves and who love Him; who will be kind to the believers, stern towards the disbelievers and who will strive in the path of Allāh without fearing the criticism of those who criticise. This is the bounty of Allāh that He grants to whoever He desires. And Allāh is All Surrounding, All Knowing." (Sūrah al-Mā'idah, 54)

48.title: Chapter 48: Warning Against Harming the Righteous, the Weak and the Poor

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Those who harm the believing men and believing women for no sin on their part, bear the burden of slander and a clear sin." (Sūrah al-Aḥzāb, 58)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Do not be harsh on the orphan. And do not drive away the beggar." (Sūrah al-Ḍuḥā, 9-10)

49.title: Chapter 49: Passing Judgement on the Outward Actions of People While Leaving Their Hidden Actions to Allah

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "But if they repent, establish ṣalāh and give zakāh, then let them go their way." (Sūrah al-Tawbah, 5)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "And fear only Me." (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 40)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Surely the grasp of your Sustainer is severe." (Sūrah al-Burūj, 12)

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Such is the grasp of your Sustainer when He seized the towns that were oppressive. Surely, His grasp is painful and severe. In them are signs for one who fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That shall be a day when people will be gathered and a day when all will be present. We have delayed it for an appointed time. When that day comes, no soul will be able to speak without His permission. Some of them are wretched and others are fortunate. As for those who are wretched, they will be in the fire, where they will shout and scream." (Sūrah Hūd, 102-106)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Allāh warns you of Himself." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 28)

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "On that day man will flee from his brother, his mother, his father, his wife and his children. On that day every one of them will be preoccupied with a predicament that will make him oblivious of others." (Sūrah 'Abasa, 34-37)

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "O people! Fear your Sustainer, for surely the earthquake of the Final Hour is a tremendous thing. When you will witness the day, every nursing mother will forget her suckling infant and every pregnant woman will abort. You will see people in a drunken stupor, yet they will not be drunk, but the punishment of Allāh is severe." (Sūrah al-Ḥajj, 1-2)
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "The one who feared standing before his Sustainer shall have two gardens." (Sūrah al-Raḥmān, 46)

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "They will face each other asking questions. They will say: 'Before this we were fearful among our families.' However, Allāh was gracious to us and saved us from the punishment of the scorching wind. Before this, we used to call to Him. He is certainly Kind, Most Merciful." (Sūrah al-Ṭūr, 25-28)
Say, 'O My servants who have wronged their souls! Do not lose hope of Allah's mercy. Surely Allah forgives all sins. Surely, He is Most forgiving, Most merciful.'
We punish only the extremely ungrateful ones.
It has been revealed to us that punishment shall be for those who reject and turn away.
My mercy encompasses everything.
Allāh quotes the words of His righteous servant: 'I surrender my affairs to Allāh. Allāh is definitely watchful over His servants. So Allāh saved him from the evil of the plots they made.'
Only those at a loss feel secure from Allāh's plan.
Indeed only the nation that commits kufr grows despondent of Allāh's mercy.
On the day when some faces will be illuminated while others will be gloomy.
Certainly your Lord Sustainer is swift in punishing. He is undoubtedly the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
Verily the righteous will be in bliss and the wicked will be in Hell.
As for him whose scales are weighty he shall be in a life of happiness. As for him whose scales are light his abode shall be the pit.

54.title: Chapter 54: The Virtue of Weeping from Fear of Allah

introVerses.text: They fall weeping on their chins and it increases their humility.
Are you astonished about this speech? And do you laugh instead of crying?

55.title: Chapter 55: The Virtue of Abstinence in this World

introVerses.text: The example of this worldly life is like the water that We send down from the sky, with which mingles the plants of the earth that man and animals eat.

Relate to them the example of this worldly life which is like water which We send down from the sky, with which mingles the plants of the earth. Thereafter they become debris, to be carried by the winds. And Allāh has power over everything. Wealth and sons are merely adornments of this worldly life. The lasting good deeds are better in the sight of your Sustainer in terms of reward and better in terms of expectations.
Know that this worldly life is merely play, futility, decoration, boasting among each other and rivalry in wealth and children.
The life of this world is mere futility and play. Without doubt, the life of the Hereafter is the true life. If only they know.

56.title: Chapter 56: The Virtue of Hunger, Living a Simple Life, and Sufficing with Little

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "They were followed by such evil successors who destroyed ṣalāh and pursued their passions. Soon they shall meet devastation. Except he who repents, believes and does good deeds. These people shall enter Paradise and they will not be oppressed in the least."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So he emerged among his people in pomp and splendour. Those who desired the life of this world gaped: 'If only we possessed what Qārūn has been given. Undoubtedly he is extremely fortunate.' Those who were granted knowledge said: 'Woe to you! Allāh's rewards are better for him who believes and does good deeds.'"
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Thereafter on that day you will certainly be questioned about the bounties."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Whoever desires the pleasures of this world, We shall speedily grant whatever We will for whoever We will in this world and then We will appoint Hell for him. He will enter it admonished and rejected."

57.title: Chapter 57: Contentment, Chastity, Restraint, and Moderation in Lifestyle

introVerses.text: The responsibility of sustaining every creature on earth rests with Allāh.

Charity is for the poor persons who are restricted in the path of Allāh, unable to move about in the land. The one who is unaware considers them to be wealthy because of their not begging. You can recognize them by their faces. They do not beg of people beseechingly.
Those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly, but are stationed in moderation between the two.
I created jinn and man only to worship Me. I neither require sustenance from them nor do I want them to feed Me.

58.title: Chapter 58: Permissibility of Taking That Which Comes Without Asking

59.title: Chapter 59: Encouraging to Earn One's Own Livelihood

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "When the ṣalāh is completed, disperse in the land and seek from Allāh's bounty."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Whatever good you spend, He will replace it."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "And whatever wealth you spend, it is for yourselves as long as you spend it to seek the pleasure of Allāh. And whatever you spend in charity, you shall receive in full and you will not be oppressed."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "And whatever good you do, surely Allāh knows about it."

61.title: Chapter 61: Prohibition of Miserliness and Greed

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "As for the one who is miserly and indifferent and who rejects the most beautiful word, We shall make the great grief easy for him. His wealth will not benefit him when he falls."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Those who are protected from the miserliness of their souls are indeed the successful ones."

62.title: Chapter 62: Giving Preference to and Comforting Others

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "They give preference to others over themselves even though they are themselves in need."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Out of love for Allāh, they feed the poor, the orphan and the captive."

63.title: Chapter 63: Competing in Matters of the Hereafter

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "It is for this that competitors should compete."

64.title: Chapter 64: The Virtue of a Grateful Wealthy Person

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "As for the one who gives, who is Allāh-fearing and who believes in the most beautiful word, We shall make the great comfort easy for him."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Far removed from it shall be the ones who are most Allāh-fearing; who spend their wealth to purify. They do not have to repay a favour to anyone except for the pleasure of their Exalted Sustainer. Soon shall they be completely satisfied."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "If you give charity openly, it is excellent indeed, but if you conceal it and convey it to the poor, it is better for you. He will expiate some of your sins. And Allāh is fully aware of what you do."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "You will never acquire righteousness until you spend of that which you love. And whatever good you spend, Allāh is certainly aware of it."

65.title: Chapter 65: Remembering Death and Curtailing Aspirations

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Every soul shall taste death and only on the day of Resurrection will you be given your rewards in full. One who is saved from the Hell-fire and entered into Paradise shall truly be successful. The life of this world is merely an enjoyment of deception."
A soul does not know what it will earn tomorrow and neither does it know in which land it will die."
When their term expires, they will not be able to delay it for a moment, nor bring it forward."

O you who believe! Let not your wealth and your children make you neglect Allāh's remembrance. Those who do this, are certainly losers. Spend from what we have provided you before death comes to any of you and then he says: 'O My Sustainer! Allow me to return so that I may perform good deeds in that which I left behind.' Never! It is merely a statement that he utters. Behind them is barzagh until the day that they are resurrected."

Has the time not come for the hearts of the believers to submit humble to Allāh's remembrance and to the truth that has been revealed. Do not become like those who were given the Book before after which a long period of time elapsed and their hearts hardened. A large number of them are sinners."

66.title: Chapter 66: Advisability of Men Visiting Graves

68.title: Chapter 68: Piety and Abstaining from the Doubtful

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "You think that the matter is trivial, whereas it is grave in Allāh's sight."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Surely your Sustainer is Ever Vigilant."

69.title: Chapter 69: Desirability of Seclusion at Times of Corruption

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So hasten towards Allāh. Verily I am a clear warner to you from Him."

70.title: Chapter 70: The Virtue of Mixing with People

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Assist each other in good deeds and piety."

71.title: Chapter 71: Humility and Being Lenient with the Believers

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Be humble to those believers who follow you."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "O believers! Whoever among you turns away from his religion, then Allāh will soon bring another nation whom He loves and who love Him; who will be kind to the believers, stern towards the disbelievers..."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "O people! We have certainly created you from a single male and female and We made you into various families and tribes so that you may recognise each other. Verily, the most honoured of you in Allāh's sight is the one with the most taqwā."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So do not ascribe purity to yourselves. He knows best who is the most pious."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "The people of A'rāf will call out to those whom they would recognise by their signs saying: 'Your masses and your pride were of no avail to you.' Were these the people regarding whom you used to take oaths that Allāh will not have mercy on them? Enter Paradise! No fear shall come upon you nor shall you grieve."

72.title: Chapter 72: The Prohibition of Pride and Self-Conceit

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "This is the home of the Hereafter which We shall assign to those who do not desire pomp on earth nor corruption. The outcome will be for those with taqwā."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Do not walk haughtily on earth."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Do not turn your face away from people and do not walk arrogantly on earth. Verily Allāh detests every arrogant boaster."

Qārūn was from Mūsā's people, but he rebelled against them. We granted him treasures, the keys of which were too heavy for a group of strong men. When his people said to him: 'Do not be boastful, for Allāh does not like the boastful ones. Seek the home of the Hereafter using the means that Allāh has given you and do not forget your portion of this world. Be good just as Allāh has been good to you. And do not seek corruption on earth, for Allāh does not like those who cause corruption.' He replied: 'I have been granted all this because of the knowledge I possess.' Did he not know that Allāh had destroyed many generations before him who were more powerful than him and larger in number? The sinners will not be questioned about their sins. So he emerged among his people in his pomp. Those who desired the world gaped: 'If only we also possessed what Qārūn has been given. Undoubtedly, he is extremely fortunate.' Those who were granted knowledge said: 'Woe to you! Allāh's reward is better for the one who has īmān and who does good deeds.' Only those who exercise patience shall receive this. So We made him and his house sink into the earth."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Verily, You are upon an exalted character."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "...and who swallow their anger, and who forgive people."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "...and swallow their anger and who forgive people. And Allāh loves those who do good."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Adopt forgiveness, instruct what is good, and ignore the ignorant ones."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Good and evil are not equal. Resist with that which is best and the one between yourself and whom there was enmity, will instantly become your bosom friend. Only the patient ones will be inspired with this. Only the most fortunate will be inspired with this."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Whoever exercises patience and forgives, this is certainly among the most resolute of matters."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "...and who forgive people. And Allāh loves those who do good."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Whoever exercises patience and forgives, this is certainly among the most resolute of matters."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Whoever exercises patience and forgives, this is certainly among the most resolute of matters."

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "And be humble to those believers who follow you."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "This is the home of the Hereafter, which We shall assign to those who do not desire pomp on earth nor corruption. The outcome shall be for those who fear."

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Allāh does not change the condition of a nation until they change the condition within themselves."

He then went to his family and returned with a fat calf. He served it to them and said: 'Are you not going to eat?'"

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "His people came running to him. Before this they had always engaged in evil deeds. He said: 'O my people! These daughters of mine are purer for you, so fear Allāh and do not disgrace me in front of my guests. Is there not a righteous man among you?'"

95.title: Chapter 95: Giving Glad Tidings and Congratulating

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So convey glad tidings to My servants who listen attentively to the speech and follow the best of it."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Their Sustainer gives them the glad tidings of His mercy, and pleasure and such gardens where they shall have everlasting bounties."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "And rejoice about the Paradise which you have been promised."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So We conveyed to him the glad tidings of an obedient son."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Indeed Our Messengers came to Ibrāhīm with glad tidings."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "His wife, standing by, laughed as We conveyed to her the glad tidings of Isḥāq, and Ya'qūb after Isḥāq."
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the chamber, 'Allāh gives you the glad tidings of Yaḥyā.'"
Allāh (ﷻ) says: "When the angels said, 'O Maryam! Indeed Allāh conveys to you the glad tidings of a word from Him. His name shall be Masīḥ.'"

96.title: Chapter 96: Saying Farewell and Advice When Departing

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Ibrāhīm and Ya'qūb advised their sons about it saying, 'O my sons! Verily Allāh has chosen this religion for you, so die only as Muslims. Or were you present when death presented itself before Ya'qūb? When he asked his sons: 'What will you worship after my death?' They replied: 'We will worship your Sustainer and the Sustainer of your forefathers, Ibrāhīm, Ismā'īl and Isḥāq, Him Who is only One Allāh. We surrender to Him only.'"

233.title: Chapter 233: The Obligation and Virtue of Ḥaj

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Ḥaj to the House is a duty that people who are able to find a way there owe to Allāh. Whoever rejects, then surely Allāh is Independent of the entire universe."

Allāh says: "Fighting is ordained for you even though you may dislike it. You may dislike something although it is good for you, or you may like something although it is bad for you. Allāh knows and you do not."
Allāh says: "Proceed when light or heavy, and exert yourselves with your wealth and lives in Allāh's way."

Allāh says: "Indeed Allāh has purchased from the believers their lives and wealth so that they may have Paradise. They fight in Allāh's path killing and being killed. This is Allāh's promise that is binding in the Tawrāh, the Injīl and the Qur'ān. Who fulfils their promise better than Allāh? So rejoice with your bargain that you have made. This is the supreme success."

Allāh says: "The believers who sit back without excuse cannot be equal to those who strive in Allāh's way with their wealth and their lives. Allāh has elevated the stages of those who strive in His way with their wealth and lives over those who sit back. Allāh has promised the most beautiful for each of them. Allāh has preferred those who strive over those who sit back by granting them a tremendous reward, many ranks, forgiveness and mercy from Him. Allāh is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful."

Allāh says: O believers! Should I not show you a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? Believe in Allāh and His Messenger and strive in Allāh's path with your wealth and lives. This is best for you if you but knew. Allāh shall forgive your sins and enter you into Paradises beneath which rivers flow and into wonderful mansions in the eternal Paradise. That is the supreme success. Another that you love is help from Allāh and a near victory. Give good news to the believers."

Allāh says: "Remember Me and I will remember you." (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 152)

Allāh says: "Continually remember your Sustainer in your heart with humility and awe, and without raising your voice. [Remember Him] by morning and evening and do not remain heedless." (Sūrah al-A'rāf, 205)
Allāh says: "And remember Allāh abundantly so that you may be successful." (Sūrah al-Jumu'ah, 10)

Allāh says: "Surely the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the believing men and the believing women, the truly devout men and the truly devout women, the truthful men and the truthful women, the patiently enduring men and the patiently enduring women, the humble men and the humble women, the charity-giving men and the charity-giving women, the fasting men and the fasting women, the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard [their chastity], the men who remember Allāh abundantly and the women who remember [Allāh abundantly] – Allāh has set aside for them forgiveness and a great reward." (Sūrah al-Aḥzāb, 35)
Allāh says: "O believers! Remember Allāh with unceasing remembrance. And continue glorifying Him at morning and evening." (Sūrah al-Aḥzāb, 41-42)

245.title: Chapter 245: Engaging in Dhikr Standing, Sitting, Lying Down and in Impurity

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of the day and night are signs for the intelligent. Those who remember Allāh standing, sitting, and lying on their sides." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 190-191)

246.title: Chapter 246: Du'a When Going to Sleep and Waking Up

247.title: Chapter 247: The Virtue of Dhikr Gatherings

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Keep yourself with those who invoke their Sustainer morning and evening, seeking His countenance. Let not your eyes overlook them." (Sūrah al-Kahf, 28)

248.title: Chapter 248: Supplications for Morning and Evening

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Continually remember your Sustainer in your heart with humility and awe, and without raising your voice. [Remember Him] by morning and evening and do not remain heedless." (Sūrah al-A'rāf, 205) The linguists say that the word "evening" refers to the time between the 'Aṣr ṣalāh and Maghrib ṣalāh.
Allāh says: "and continue proclaiming the praises of your Sustainer before sunrise and before sunset." (Sūrah Ṭā Hā, 130)
Allāh says: "and glorify the praises of your Sustainer in the evening and morning." (Sūrah al-Mu'min, 55)

Allāh says: "In those houses which Allāh has ordained to be raised and that His name be remembered therein – remembering Him therein morning and evening. Men whom neither trade nor sale can divert from the remembrance of Allāh." (Sūrah al-Nūr, 36-37)
Allāh says: "We subjugated the mountains with him, expressing [Our] purity in the evening and the morning." (Sūrah Ṣād, 18)

249.title: Chapter 249: Du'as When Going to Sleep

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Surely in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of the day and night are signs for the intelligent. Those who remember Allāh standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth." (Sūrah Āl 'Imrān, 3: 190-191)
Allāh says: "Your Sustainer says: 'Call to Me so that I may respond to your call.'" (Sūrah Mu'min, 60)
Allāh says: "Call on your Sustainer humbly and secretly. He does not like those who transgress the bounds." (Sūrah al-A'rāf, 55)
Allāh says: "When My servants ask you concerning Me, I am near. I accept the supplication of the supplicant when he supplicates to Me." (Sūrah al-Baqarah, 186)
Allāh says: "Who is it that responds to the distressed when he calls Him, and removes the hardship?" (Sūrah al-Naml, 62)

251.title: The Virtue of Supplicating for Someone in Their Absence

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Those who came after them, say: 'O our Sustainer! Forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.'"
Allāh says: "Seek forgiveness for your sins and for the believing men and believing women."
Allāh says about Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): "O our Sustainer! Forgive me, my parents, and all the believers on the day when the reckoning takes place."

253.title: Chapter on the Miracles and Virtues of the Awliya' (Friends of Allah)

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Behold! Verily for the friends of Allāh there shall be no fear, nor shall they grieve. Those who have īmān and adopt taqwā. For them shall be glad tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is nothing that can change the words of Allāh. This is the greatest success."
Allāh says: "Shake the trunk of the date palm towards you, causing fresh ripened dates to fall on you. So eat, drink..."

Allāh says: "Whenever Zakariyyā went into the chamber, he found food by her. He said: 'O Maryam, from where did you get this?' She replied: 'It is from Allāh. Allāh provides for whom He pleases without count.'"

Allāh says: "When you have separated yourselves from them and what they worship besides Allāh, then seek refuge in the cave. May your Sustainer shower His mercy upon you and make your objectives easy to reach. You will see that when the sun rose, it would pass by their cave on the right and when it would set, it would pass by on the left."

254.title: Chapter on the Prohibition of Backbiting and the Command to Safeguard the Tongue

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "Never backbite each other. Would any one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother, which you so detest? Fear Allāh. Allāh is certainly All Forgiving, Most Merciful."
Allāh says: "Do not pursue what you have no knowledge about. Indeed questioning shall take place with regard to the ears, the eyes and the hearts."
Allāh says: "Whenever a word escapes, there is a guard ready by him."

introVerses.text: Allāh says: "When they hear futile talk, they turn away from it."

Allāh says: "Indeed questioning shall take place with regard to the ears, the eyes and the hearts."

Allāh says: "When you see those who engross themselves with Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in some other talk. Should Shaiṭān cause you to forget, then after recalling, do not sit with the unjust people."

If they had referred the matter to the Messenger and to those of them who have understanding, it would surely be known to those of them who investigate the matter. If it were not for Allāh's grace and mercy on you, you would follow Shaiṭān except for a few.
O you who believe! If any sinner brings you any news, then verify it, lest you should harm any nation unknowingly and then become remorseful.

372.title: Chapter on what Allah has prepared for the believers in Paradise

introVerses.text: Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Those who adopt taqwā will definitely be in gardens and springs. Enter it with peace and safety. We shall remove any ill-feelingys that may be in their breasts. As brothers they will be seated on couches, facing each other. No difficulty shall afflict them there, neither will they be removed from there."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "O My servants! You shall have no fear today, neither will you grieve. Those who believed in Our verses and were obedient. You and your spouses should enter into Paradise happily. Bowls and cups of gold will be passed around between them and in Paradise there shall be whatever the heart desires and whatever pleases the eye. You will live there forever. That is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit because of the good deeds you carried out. In it you will have an abundance of fruit to eat."

Allāh (ﷻ) says: "Verily those with taqwā shall be in a place of peace. In gardens and springs. They will wear clothing of fine silk and thick silk, and will be seated facing each other. This is how it will be. We will also marry them to fair large-eyed damsels. In comfort, they will call for all types of fruit there. They will not taste death there except for the first death. Allāh will save them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire as a favour from your Sustainer. This is the greatest success."

1.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Actions are gauged by intentions. Each person will receive (the reward for) what he intended. One who emigrates to Allāh and His Messenger, his emigration is indeed to Allāh and His Messenger. One who emigrates to acquire something of the world or to marry a woman, his emigration is to that to which he emigrated." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches that actions are judged by their intentions. A man became known as "Muhājir Umm Qais" because he migrated to marry a woman, not for Allāh's sake. Imām al-Bukhārī chose to begin his Ṣaḥīḥ with this ḥadīth to emphasize sincerity. Scholars agree that Niyyah (intention) is founded in the heart and should not be verbalized. Ikhlāṣ (sincerity) is essential—one should seek only the Pleasure of Allāh.

2.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "An army will advance in order to attack the Ka'bah. When they reach an even plain, all of them will be swallowed into the earth." I asked, "O Messenger of Allāh! How will all of them be swallowed up when among them were traders and others who were not really part of them?" He replied, "All of them will be swallowed up and they will be resurrected according to their intentions." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
2.commentary: Everyone will be rewarded or punished according to their intentions. This ḥadīth warns about the danger of accompanying sinners—one who joins them by choice invites punishment upon himself. One should accompany the pious and avoid the gatherings of oppressors.

3.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "There is no migration after the conquest (of Makkah), but there is jihād and intention. When you are commanded to go in jihād, you should go." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
3.commentary: Hijrah (migration) was obligatory in early Islām. After Makkah was conquered, this obligation fell away while jihād and intention remained. However, it remains compulsory for Muslims to migrate from lands where they cannot practise their religion. The ḥadīth gives glad tidings that Makkah will forever remain a land of Islām.

4.text: We were once with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on a military expedition when he said, 'There are some people who remained behind in Madīnah. They were with you when you traversed any path or crossed any valley; it was only that illness kept them back.'" Another narration has: "However, they will share the reward with you." (Muslim) Bukhārī narrates from Anas (رضي الله عنه) who said: "We returned from the battle of Tabūk with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) when he said, 'There are some people whom we left behind in Madīnah, but we did not traverse any path or any valley without them sharing the reward with us. A valid excuse kept them back.'" (Bukhārī)
4.commentary: A person who had the noble intention of participating in jihād but was withheld by a valid reason will receive the same reward as the mujāhidīn. The noble intention of a believer is equivalent in reward to his good action.

5.narrator: Ma'n ibn Yazīd ibn al-Akhnas (رضي الله عنهم)
5.text: He, his father and grandfather were all Ṣaḥābah—narrates: "My father, Yazīd, put aside some dīnārs to give in charity and placed them in the hand of a person in the masjid. I came along, took the dīnārs and brought them to him. He said: 'By Allāh, I did not intend giving them to you.' We then went and presented the case before the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). He said: 'O Yazīd, you will receive what you intended, and, O Ma'n, you may keep what you took.'" (Bukhārī)
5.commentary: Yazīd (رضي الله عنه) was rewarded because he intended to give charity to a needy person. Optional charity may be given to one's offspring, and it is permissible to appoint a representative to distribute charity on one's behalf.

6.narrator: Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (رضي الله عنه)
6.text: One of the ten Ṣaḥābah who were given glad tidings of Paradise, narrates: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) visited me in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage because I was afflicted with a serious illness. I said: 'O Messenger of Allāh, you can see the severity of my illness and I am a wealthy person with no heirs except a daughter. Should I give two thirds of my wealth in charity?' He replied: 'No.' I asked, 'A half, O Messenger of Allāh?' He replied: 'No.' I asked, 'A third, O Messenger of Allāh?' He replied: 'A third is fine, but even a third is a lot (or much). It is better for you to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor and begging from people. You will most certainly be rewarded for whatever you spend for the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ), even for the morsel of food which you place in your wife's mouth.' I asked: 'O Messenger of Allāh, will I be left behind after my companions (leave Makkah Mukarramah)?' He replied: 'You will not be left behind, for whatever deeds you do for the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ), will increase you in status and rank. And perhaps you will be left behind so that some people will benefit from you while others will be harmed by you. O Allāh, complete for my Ṣaḥābah their emigration and do not let them turn back on their heels. However, the unfortunate Sa'd ibn Khaulah.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) lamented over him because he passed away in Makkah." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
6.commentary: A testator is allowed to bequeath up to one third of his estate. One will be rewarded for spending on family, and even for leaving wealth for heirs with the intention to please Allāh. A leader should visit and console those who are ill.

7.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) neither looks at your bodies nor at your appearances; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds." (Muslim)
7.commentary: Allāh (ﷻ) does not reward people based on their outer form or complexion. He rewards an action when one's heart is sincere and purified of evil qualities. One should strive to purify the heart because a heart that is pure will rectify the action and guide it toward success.

8.narrator: Abdullāh ibn Qays al Ash'arī (رضي الله عنه)
8.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was asked about a person who fights to display his bravery, a person who fights to protect his family honour and a person who fights to show off and whether any of them were in the cause of Allāh? The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) replied: 'The person who fights so that the word of Allāh may reign supreme is the one who is in the cause of Allāh.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
8.commentary: The true mujāhidīn are those who only fight so that the religion of Allāh (ﷻ) may reign supreme. One who fights seeking the reward of the Hereafter or the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ) is also included. A person should be careful not to succumb to base desires or worldly motives when engaging in any noble action.

9.narrator: Nufay' ibn Ḥārith al-Thaqafī (رضي الله عنه)
9.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When two Muslims attack each other with their swords, then both the killer and the one who is killed will be in the Hell-fire." I asked, "O Messenger of Allāh, I can understand this with regard to the killer, but what about the one who is killed?" He (ﷺ) replied: "He was eager to kill his companion." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
9.commentary: A person will be held accountable for his firm intention to perpetrate an evil action. If the thought of a sin crosses a person's mind and he rejects it, it will be forgiven. But if he affirms his intention and utilises the means to accomplish it, it will be recorded as an evil. This ḥadīth warns against Muslims fighting each other.

10.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The ṣalāh which a person offers in congregation is more than twenty times superior to his ṣalāh in his business or his home. The reason for this is that when a person performs a perfect wuḍū', proceeds to the masjid with the sole intention of offering ṣalāh and nothing except ṣalāh, then for every step he takes, his rank is elevated by a degree and a sin is wiped off his record, until he enters the masjid. Once he enters the masjid, he is considered to be in ṣalāh as long as the ṣalāh keeps him (in the masjid). The angels continue making du'ā' for him as long as he remains seated at the place where he offered his ṣalāh, saying: 'O Allāh, be merciful to him! O Allāh, forgive him! O Allāh, accept his repentance!' This continues as long as he does not harm anyone and as long as he does not nullify his wuḍū'." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
10.commentary: Ṣalāh in congregation is superior to the ṣalāh that is performed individually by twenty-five or twenty-seven times as stated in other aḥādīth. The sincerity of intention whilst performing ṣalāh will determine the exact reward. For every step to the masjid, one's rank is elevated and a sin is obliterated.

11.text: From the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) who narrates from Allāh (ﷻ): "Allāh (ﷻ) recorded the good and evil deeds and He then explained them: Whoever intends doing a good deed but does not carry it out, Allāh records it as a complete good deed. However, if he intends doing a good deed and then carries it out, Allāh records ten good deeds to seven hundred folds, and even more. Whoever intends doing an evil deed but does not carry it out, Allāh records it as a full good deed. But if he intends doing an evil deed and carries it out, Allāh records it as one evil deed." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
11.commentary: This is a Ḥadīth al-Qudsī (Sacred Tradition), communicated by Allāh to the Prophet (ﷺ) through inspiration. It demonstrates Allāh's immense compassion and generosity—rewarding a person for intending good even if not executed, and recording only one sin if evil is committed but a good deed if he refrains out of fear of Allāh.

12.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: 'Three people from a nation of the past were walking and took refuge in a cave for the night. A rock fell from the mountain and blocked the mouth of the cave. They said: The only thing that will save you from this rock is your supplication to Allāh (ﷻ) by virtue of your good deeds.' One of them said: 'O Allāh, I had extremely old parents and it was my habit that I never gave milk to my family and slaves before giving it to them. One day I went far off in search of grazing pastures and I returned late in the evening. I found that my parents had already fallen asleep. I milked their drink as was my habit and brought it to them. I did not want to awaken them from their sleep and I also did not want to give it to my family and slaves before giving it to my parents. I remained standing with the bowl in my hands, waiting for them to wake up until dawn broke and the children were crying at my feet out of hunger. They then both awoke and drank their milk. O Allāh, if I did this for Your pleasure, then rescue us from this cave by removing this rock.' It opened slightly, but they were still unable to get out. The second person said: 'O Allāh, I had a cousin who I loved passionately.' Another narration has: 'I loved her as passionately as a man could love a woman.' 'I tried to seduce her but she refused me. Eventually, one year she was reduced to poverty and was forced to come to me for assistance. I gave her 120 dīnārs on condition that she yield herself to me. She agreed, but when I had full control over her – and in another narration – when I was about to engage in sexual relations with her, she said: Fear Allāh and do not break the seal unlawfully. So I turned away from her despite the fact that I loved her most passionately; and I let her keep the money I had given her. O Allāh, if I did that to seek Your pleasure, then remove the distress in which we are.' The rock moved aside a bit further but they were still unable to get out. The third one said: 'O Allāh! I hired some labourers and paid them their wages except one of them who departed without taking his due. I invested his money in business and the business prospered greatly. After a long time, he came to me and said: O slave of Allāh! Pay me my dues. I said: All that you see is yours – camels, cattle, goats and slaves. He said: O slave of Allāh! Do not mock at me. I assured him that I was not joking. So he took all the things and went away. He spared nothing. O Allāh! If I did so seeking Your pleasure, then relieve us of our distress.' The rock then moved aside and they walked out freely.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
12.commentary: It is permissible to pray through our virtuous deeds (tawassul). Preference should be given to the service of parents. To abstain from sins out of fear of Allāh is a highly meritorious act. Labourers should always be treated fairly. Any supplication which is made sincerely, and with a real sense of humbleness, is granted by Allāh.

13.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: 'By Allāh, I seek forgiveness from Allāh and I turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.'" (Bukhārī)
13.commentary: The abundant repentance of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was not because of any sin; rather, it serves as encouragement and a lesson to the Ummah to repent and seek forgiveness in abundance. If the Prophet (ﷺ), whose past and future sins were forgiven, repented so frequently, it is even more necessary for his followers to do so.

14.narrator: Al-Agharr ibn Yasār al Muzanī (رضي الله عنه)
14.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "O people! Turn in repentance to Allāh (ﷻ) and seek forgiveness from Him for I turn to Him in repentance one hundred times a day." (Muslim)
14.commentary: This ḥadīth, like the previous one, encourages us to hasten in repentance. The figures of one hundred in this ḥadīth and seventy in the previous one are not of essence; rather they simply indicate that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) engaged in abundant repentance.

15.text: Anas ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه), the attendant of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his camel after having lost it in a desert land." (Bukhārī, Muslim) Another narration of Muslim has: "Allāh (ﷻ) is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a person who was on his camel in a desert land and it slipped away from him with his food and drink still loaded on it. He becomes despondent, goes to a tree and lies down in its shade, having no hope of finding it. While he is lying down, he suddenly sees his camel standing before him. He holds it by its reins and then exclaims out of intense joy: 'O Allāh, you are my slave and I am Your Lord,' erring because of his intense joy at finding his camel." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
15.commentary: Allāh (ﷻ) is intensely pleased when His servant turns to Him in repentance. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), the perfect teacher, utilised an analogy to simplify the idea so that people could understand it. When the urge to turn to Allāh enters the heart, one should hasten in repentance because our life in this world is to please Him.

16.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) stretches out His hand at night so that one who sinned during the day may turn to Him in repentance and He stretches out His hand in the day so that one who sinned during the night may turn to Him in repentance, until the sun rises from the west." (Muslim)
16.commentary: "Allāh spreading out His hand" means that Allāh spreads His mercy and opens the door of repentance. Repentance is accepted by Allāh (ﷻ) as long as the doors of repentance remain open. They will close when Qiyāmah begins with the rising of the sun from the west.

17.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) will accept the repentance of anyone who turns in repentance to Him before the time when the sun rises from the west." (Muslim)
17.commentary: Allāh (ﷻ) accepts the repentance of a person out of His mercy and kindness and the doors of His repentance will remain open until Qiyāmah. The scholars of tafsīr explain that "some of your Lord's signs" in Sūrah al-An'ām refer to the rising of the sun from the west.

18.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) accepts the repentance of a person as long as his soul does not reach his throat (at the time of death)." (Tirmidhī)
18.commentary: يُغَرْغِرْ literally means to place a drink into the mouth and push it to the back of the throat without swallowing it. It refers to the state of a person who is in his final moments of life and his soul has reached the bottom part of his throat. Repentance is only valid if it takes place before a person reaches this state when life is slipping away.

19.text: Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh narrates: I went to Ṣafwān ibn 'Assāl (رضي الله عنه) to ask him the ruling about masaḥ (passing of wet hands) over leather socks. He asked me: 'Why have you come, O Zirr?' I replied: 'To seek knowledge.' He said: 'The angels spread out their wings for the seeker of knowledge out of pleasure at what he is seeking.' ... 'We were once on a journey with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) ... The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) continued talking to us until he mentioned a door in the west whose width is (or in whose width a rider will continue to ride for) forty or seventy years.' Sufyān, one of the narrators, said: 'This door is in the direction of Syria. Allāh (ﷻ) created it the day He created the heavens and the earth. It is open for repentance and it will not be shut until the sun rises from there.' (Tirmidhī)
19.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that the doors of repentance are open and will remain open until Qiyāmah. Those who seek Islāmic knowledge should know that Islāmic knowledge is as vast as an ocean that has no shore. A person shall be with those whom he loved on the day of Qiyāmah.

20.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Amongst the nations before you there was a person who had killed ninety-nine people. He inquired who was the most knowledgeable person on the earth and was referred to a monk. He went to him and informed him that he had killed ninety-nine people and asked whether there was any possibility of repentance for him. The monk said: 'No,' so he killed the monk and thereby increased the number he had killed to one hundred. He again inquired who was the most knowledgeable person on earth and was referred to a scholar. He informed him that he had killed a hundred people and asked whether there was any possibility of repentance for him. The scholar replied: 'Yes. Who can come between you and repentance? Go to such and such place because there are people there who are engaged in the worship of Allāh (ﷻ). Join them in the worship of Allāh (ﷻ) and do not return to your land because it is an evil place.' The man then departed for that land, but when he reached halfway, death overcame him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed among themselves with regard to his fate. The angels of mercy said: 'He came in repentance, turning with his heart to Allāh (ﷻ).' The angels of punishment said: 'He never did any good.' An angel then came to them in the form of a human being and they appointed him as an arbitrator between them. He said to them: 'Measure the distance between the two places and to whichever of the two he is closer, he will be considered to be of that place.' They measured the distance and found him to be closer to the place to which he was going, so the angels of mercy took his life." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
20.commentary: This ḥadīth serves as a tremendous source of hope for those seeking the mercy and forgiveness of Allāh (ﷻ). The killer's sincere desire to purify himself led him to a monk who wrongly advised that the doors of mercy were closed to him. The scholar's knowledge guided the man to the truth. This establishes the virtue of knowledge over worship. A person should abstain from befriending sinners and should instead strive to remain in the company of the pious.

21.text: 'Abdullāh ibn Ka'b ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه), who was from among the sons of Ka'b and who served as a guide to him when he became blind, narrates: I heard (my father) Ka'b ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه) narrating his story when he did not join the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabūk... [The lengthy ḥadīth describing how Ka'b stayed behind from the expedition, his honesty before the Prophet (ﷺ), and the boycott by the Muslims for fifty nights until his repentance was accepted by revelation]... Ka'b (رضي الله عنه) said: 'When I greeted the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), his face was beaming with pleasure and he said: "Rejoice with the best day you have ever seen since your mother gave you birth." I said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Is this (good news) from you or from Allāh?" He said: "No, it is from Allāh (ﷻ)."' (Bukhārī, Muslim)
21.commentary: A Muslim should always speak the truth even if he has to face troubles and turmoil for it because the Pleasure of Allāh lies in truth. One must avoid at all costs the attitude of hypocrites because eventually one is ruined by it. In spite of hardship and stringency, one must take part in jihād. It is lawful to give something by way of gift and reward to a person who congratulates in the events of happiness.

22.narrator: Imrān ibn Ḥuṣayn al-Khuzā'ī (رضي الله عنه)
22.text: A woman from the tribe of Juhaynah came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) while she was pregnant from (Zinā) adultery and said to him: "O Messenger of Allāh! I have committed an offense liable to Ḥadd (prescribed punishment), so exact the execution of the sentence." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) called her guardian and said to him: "Treat her kindly. Bring her to me after the delivery of the child." That man complied with the orders. At last the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded to carry out the sentence. Her clothes were secured around her and she was stoned to death. The Prophet (ﷺ) led her funeral prayers. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) submitted: "O Messenger of Allāh! She committed Zinā and you have performed funeral prayer for her?" He replied: "Verily, she made repentance which would suffice for seventy of the people of Al-Madīnah if it is divided among them. Can there be any higher degree of repentance than that she sacrificed her life voluntarily to win the Pleasure of Allāh, the Exalted?" (Muslim)
22.commentary: This ḥadīth confirms the validity of the punishment of Rajm (stoning) for the adulterer. It highlights the merit of sincere repentance. It is permissible to perform the funeral prayer of one who has been guilty of major sins, provided he has not been taking them as lawful. A pregnant woman cannot be punished with Rajm until she gives birth to the child and the period specified for suckling the baby is completed.

23.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If the son of Adam possesses a valley full of gold, he would love to have two valleys, but nothing will fill his mouth except the soil of the grave. Allāh (ﷻ) accepts the repentance of those who repent to Him." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
23.commentary: Greed for wealth makes a person blind and overpowers him until he does not distinguish between ḥalāl and ḥarām. His only objective is to amass more wealth and he only realizes his foolishness when his belly is filled with the sand of his grave. The soul of a man in search of wealth is similar to the fire of Hell—when fuel is added to it, it will say: "Is there any more to come?" (Sūrah Qāf, 30)

24.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) laughs in pleasure at two people: one of whom kills the other, yet both of them enter Paradise. One fights for the cause of Allāh (ﷻ) and is killed (martyred). Allāh (ﷻ) then turns towards the killer who then embraces Islām and is martyred." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
24.commentary: The two people entering Paradise does not necessarily mean they will have equal status; this depends on their respective actions. One should never be despondent of the mercy of Allāh (ﷻ), as He is Most Forgiving. Allāh (ﷻ) pardons the sin of disbelief after a person accepts Islām and He accepts a Muslim's repentance from major sins.

25.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Purity is half of faith. (The phrase) al-Ḥamdulillāh fills the scale. (The phrases) Subḥānallāh and al-Ḥamdulillāh fill (or the reward fills) all the space between the heavens and the earth. Ṣalāh is a light. Charity is a proof. Patience is an illumination. The Qur'ān is a proof for you or against you. Every person departs in the morning and sells his soul by either freeing it (from punishment) or destroying it." (Muslim)
25.commentary: This ḥadīth encapsulates foundational principles of Islām: ṭahārah (purity), ṣalāh, charity, patience and obedience to the Qur'ān. Patience is described as ḍiyā' (illumination)—a struggle that provides light and guidance, unlike the easy light of the sun. The Qur'ān will serve as proof for or against a person depending on whether he practises its teachings.

26.text: Some people from the Anṣār (Helpers) asked the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) for something so he gave them. They again asked him and he again gave them. This continued until whatever he had was depleted. When he had given everything, he said to them: "I will never withhold from you what I possess. However, Allāh (ﷻ) gives chastity to the one who seeks it, Allāh (ﷻ) gives independence to the one who seeks it and Allāh (ﷻ) gives patience to the one who exercises patience. No person has been given a gift that is better and greater than that of patience." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
26.commentary: This ḥadīth highlights the generosity of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)—he never refused when asked. Yet he encouraged contentment and independence, explaining that begging is not advisable. A Muslim should avoid desiring what others possess and should be patient in times of difficulty. Whoever strives for patience will be granted it by Allāh (ﷻ).

27.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Truly excellent is the situation of a believer! Everything is to his advantage and this is enjoyed by none except him. When he experiences happiness, he is grateful and it is to his advantage. When he experiences distress, he is patient and it is to his advantage." (Muslim)
27.commentary: A believer is tested on two types of occasions: happiness and sadness. His gratitude at the time of happiness results in an increase of the bounty in this world and reward in the Hereafter. His patience at the time of difficulty means that he accepts the decision of Allāh (ﷻ) and is hopeful for reward from Him. In contrast, one with incomplete faith becomes anxious and angry when difficulty strikes.

28.text: When the health of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) began to deteriorate, the pangs of death began overpowering him. Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها) said: 'Oh! How painful the pangs of death are to my father!' He said: 'After this day your father will experience no more pain.' When he passed away, she said: 'O my father! You replied to the call of your Sustainer. O my father! The Garden of Firdaus is your abode. O my father! We shall convey this news to Jibra'īl.' When the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was buried, Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها) said: 'Did it please you to throw sand over the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)?'" (Bukhārī)
28.commentary: This ḥadīth describes the patience of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) during his final moments and the patience and restraint of Fāṭimah (رضي الله عنها). He consoled her saying that death for a believer is a release from trials of this world. Her statement about throwing sand was an expression of grief, not an objection to the burial.

29.text: Usāmah ibn Zayd ibn Ḥārithah (رضي الله عنهما), the freed slave, beloved and the son of the beloved of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), narrates: "The daughter of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sent a message to him saying: 'My son is on the verge of death. Please come.' He sent a message conveying his greetings and said: 'To Allāh alone belongs all that He takes and to Him belongs all that He gives; everything has an appointed term with Him, so you should exercise patience and be hopeful of reward (for your patience).' She then sent a message with an oath that he should come to her. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) proceeded with Sa'd ibn 'Ubādah, Mu'ādh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Zayd ibn Thābit and other Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم). The child was given to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) who placed it in his lap while it was panting for breath. The eyes of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) began flowing with tears. Sa'd (رضي الله عنه) asked: 'What is this, O Messenger of Allāh?' He replied: 'This is mercy which Allāh (ﷻ) has placed in the hearts of His servants.' Another narration has: 'This is mercy which Allāh (ﷻ) places in whichever of His servants He wills. Allāh (ﷻ) is merciful to those of His servants who are merciful to others.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
29.commentary: This provides a perfect formula for condolences: "To Allāh alone belongs all that He takes and to Him belongs all that He gives." This shifts focus from the loss to the Ownership of Allāh (ﷻ). True patience (ṣabr) is accompanied by iḥtisāb (seeking reward), transforming a painful experience into worship. Shedding tears is not contrary to patience—only wailing and uncontrolled behaviour is prohibited.

30.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Among those before you, there was a king who had a magician. When he reached old age, he said to the king: 'I have become old, so send me a young man to whom I may teach this magic.' So the king sent him a young man to teach. On his way to the magician, he saw a monk. He sat down in the monk's company, heard his speech and liked it. Whenever he went to the magician, he would sit in the company of the monk. When he would reach the magician, the latter would beat him (for sitting in the monk's company). He complained to the monk who said: 'When you fear the magician's beating, say to him: My family delayed me. And when you fear your family complaining, say to them: The magician delayed me.' He continued like this for a time. One day, he came across a huge animal that was obstructing the people's path. He said to himself: 'Today I will find out who is better, the magician or the monk.' He picked up a rock and said: 'O Allāh! If the monk's ways are more beloved to You than the magician's, then kill this animal so that the people may walk the path.' He then threw the rock at the animal and killed it and the people were again able to use the path..." ... [The ḥadīth continues describing how the boy healed the blind and the lepers, the king's attempts to kill him failed until the boy instructed the king to say 'In the name of Allāh, the Lord of the youth' before shooting him with an arrow. When the king did so and the boy died, all the people believed in Allāh.] ... "So the king assembled all the people on a single plain, suspended the youth from a tree, took an arrow from his quiver, placed it in the centre of the bow and said: 'In the name of Allāh, the Lord of the youth.' He then shot it and it struck the youth's temple. The youth placed his hand on his temple and passed away. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the youth.' The king was told: 'By Allāh, what you feared has come to pass. The people have brought faith.' So the king ordered trenches to be dug on the roads and fires were ignited therein. He then announced: 'Whoever does not renounce his religion will be forcefully cast into the fire' (or will be ordered: 'Jump into the fire'). They obeyed the order until a woman with an infant came forward. She hesitated to jump into it and the infant said to her: 'O my mother! Exercise patience for you are on the truth!'" (Muslim)
30.commentary: This profound ḥadīth teaches the importance of steadfastness in faith even in the face of death. The boy sacrificed his life to guide his people to the Truth, showing that ultimate victory is spiritual, not worldly. The story also establishes the virtue of knowledge over mere worship, and that Allāh (ﷻ) responds to the sincere supplication of His servants.

31.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed by a woman who was crying at a grave. He said: "Fear Allāh and exercise patience." She said: "Leave me alone. You have not been afflicted with a calamity like mine." She did not know that it was the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). When someone informed her: "That was the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)," she came to the door of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and, finding no guards there, she said to him: "I did not recognize you." He said: "The time for patience is at the onset of the calamity." (Bukhārī, Muslim). A narration of Muslim has: "She was crying over the loss of her child."
31.commentary: Patience at the onset of a calamity is noteworthy because the stress associated with it subsides over time. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) did not respond angrily when the woman unknowingly rebuked him; rather, he preferred to advise her towards patience. The fact that she found no guards at his door was evidence of his humility and simplicity.

32.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) says: 'When I take away a beloved of My believing servant and he exercises patience in anticipation of reward, then he can have no recompense from Me except Paradise.'" (Bukhārī)
32.commentary: This Ḥadīth al-Qudsī teaches that patience in the face of a calamity is a sign of complete īmān. The prerequisites for acquiring the reward specified here are that a person should exercise patience, be pleased with the decision of Allāh (ﷻ) and be hopeful of divine reward.

33.text: She asked the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) about a plague. He informed her that it is a punishment, which Allāh (ﷻ) sends to whomever He wills, but He makes it a source of mercy for the believers. Any servant who is caught in a plague and remains there patiently, anticipating reward and having full conviction that nothing can afflict him except that which Allāh (ﷻ) has destined for him, shall receive the reward of a martyr." (Bukhārī)
33.commentary: This ḥadīth explains the reward of a person who patiently endures a plague or fatal sickness.
