399.commentary: The Fire will envelope the bodies of people in varying degrees according to the severity of their sins. However, the part of the body not covered in fire will also boil due to the intensity of the fire afflicting the remaining portions of the body.

400.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The people will assemble before the Sustainer of the worlds and some of them will be submerged in their perspiration up to half their ears." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
400.commentary: This ḥadīth describes another of the terrifying scenes of the day of Qiyāmah that will be unlike anything in this world. Everybody will rise from their graves and stand before Allāh (ﷻ) to receive their reward or punishment. The scholars have provided various answers to how people will be immersed in different levels of perspiration when everybody will be standing together. Allāh (ﷻ) may create such a situation by causing the ground to rise under the feet of some people, forming a mound that will keep them higher than others. It is also possible that Allāh (ﷻ) will cause each person's sweat to be confined around him - defying the laws of physics - just as He held back the water of the Red Sea for Mūsā (عليه السلام) and his companions.

401.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) addressed us in a sermon the like of which I have never heard. He said: 'If you only knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much.' On hearing this, the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) covered their faces and began weeping." (Bukhārī, Muslim). Another narration has: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) heard something about his Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم). He therefore addressed them saying: 'Paradise and the Hell-fire were presented before me and I have not seen a day like this day in respect of good and evil. If you only knew what I know, you will laugh little and cry much.' Never did the Ṣaḥābah experience a more severe day than this. They covered their heads and began weeping."
401.commentary: In this ḥadīth, fear is emphasised over hope, exhorting us to cry excessively out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) and to avoid excessive laughter, which shows hard-heartedness and negligence of the Hereafter. The statement, "if you only knew what I know," refers to the difficulties associated with death and the grave, the terrors of the Hereafter, the punishment for those who sin and the torment of Hell. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was shown Paradise and Hell-fire. This could mean that these two places were described to him in such detail that he could picture them. However, it is more likely that they were shown to him physically, by removing the barriers between them and himself.

402.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "On the day of Qiyāmah, the sun will be brought close to the creation until it will be one mile away from them." Sulaym ibn 'Āmir (رضي الله عنه), the narrator, narrates from al-Miqdād (رضي الله عنه) saying: "By Allāh, I do not know what he meant by a mile (mīl). Was he referring to the distance on land, or was he referring to a poker-stick dipped in antimony which is applied to the eye?" (The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) continues): "The people will be submerged in perspiration according to their deeds. Some will be submerged up to their ankles, others up to their knees, others up to their hips and there will be those whose mouths the perspiration will bridle." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then pointed to his mouth with his hand. (Muslim)
402.commentary: The sun, according to astronomers, is approximately 93 million miles away from the earth. The heat of the sun travels across this great distance and warms our planet, sometimes causing extremely high temperatures that are unbearable to human beings. On the day of Qiyāmah, when everybody will be standing in wait for the accounting of deeds, the sun will be brought one mile above our heads, or even closer. People will sink in their sweat in proportion to their deeds. The only hope we have is to be included in the shade that will be provided by Allāh (ﷻ) to His chosen servants.

403.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "On the day of Qiyāmah people will perspire to such an extent that their perspiration will seep into the ground as deep as seventy cubits and it will bridle them until it reaches their ears." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
403.commentary: As stated in previous aḥādīth, people will be immersed in different levels of perspiration. The worst condition will be that of the disbelievers, then those who committed major sins and so on. The Messengers (عليهم السلام), the martyrs and the fortunate among the believing men and women will be protected from this phenomenon altogether and will enjoy the privilege of Allāh (ﷻ)'s shade. May Allāh (ﷻ) make us from among them. According to this ḥadīth, the perspiration of some people will seep into the ground seventy cubits deep.

404.text: We were with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) when he suddenly heard the sound of something falling. He asked us: 'Do you know what that was?' We replied: 'Allāh and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It was a rock which was thrown into the Hell-fire seventy years ago. It continued falling into the Hell-fire and has now reached the bottom, resulting in the sound you just heard.'" (Muslim)
404.commentary: The ḥadīth highlights the enormous depth of Hell and this necessitates that its punishment will be severe and excruciating. May Allāh (ﷻ) save us! According to this ḥadīth, the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) also heard the sound along with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). This would then be counted as a miracle of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم), similar to the incidents when the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) heard the crying of a tree stump and the tasbīḥ of pebbles in the hand of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ).

405.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) will speak with every single one of you without an interpreter between you and Him. You will look to your right and will see nothing except the deeds that you had sent forward. You will look to your left and will see nothing except the deeds that you had sent forward. You will look in front of you and will see nothing except the Hell-fire directly facing you. You should therefore safeguard yourselves from the Hell-fire even if it is with half a date." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
405.commentary: This ḥadīth was discussed in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 139. The person will look to his left and right in order to find a path of safety from the Fire just as a person in this world anxiously looks around him when he is in danger. "You should therefore safeguard yourselves from the Hell-fire even if it is with half a date," means that one should seek salvation from Hell by giving even small amounts of charity. It could also mean that one should seek salvation from Hell by avoiding indulging in even small amounts of oppression and sin.

406.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "I see that which you do not see. The sky groans and it has every right to groan. There is not an empty space of even four fingers without an angel placing his forehead in prostration before Allāh (ﷻ). By Allāh, if you only knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much. You would not take any delight from women in beds and you would go out into the paths, seeking the help of Allāh (ﷻ)." (Tirmidhī)
406.commentary: The sky does not literally groan in pain. Rather, this sound emphasises the abundance of angels in prostration in awe of Allah (ﷻ). It is similar to the example of a truck creaking due to a heavy load. The skies are filled with righteous actions and angels who perform righteous actions. Imām Shāfi'ī (رحمه الله) deduces from this that the sky is superior to the earth and that places have different virtues according to the actions that are committed within them. The ḥadīth also points to the great number of angels, who are always engaged in the worship of Allāh (ﷻ). The phrase "if you only knew what I know," means that if we knew of the immense majesty of Allāh (ﷻ) and His severe punishment for those who disobey Him, we would laugh less and cry more, out of fear.

407.narrator: Abū Barzah Naḍlah ibn 'Ubayd al-Aslamī (رضي الله عنه)
407.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The feet of a person will not move (on the day of Qiyāmah) until he is asked about his life and how he spent it, about his knowledge and how he utilized it, about his wealth and from where he acquired it and where he spent it and about his body and how he wore it out." (Tirmidhī)
407.commentary: On the day of Qiyāmah, every person will stand before Allāh (ﷻ) to be accountable for his deeds. Nobody will take a step towards Paradise or Hell-fire until four questions are put to him. The Messengers (عليهم السلام) are of course exempted from this, as well as those fortunate believers who will enter Paradise without any accountability.

408.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) recited this verse: "On that day, the earth will narrate its news," and he then asked: "Do you know what its news is?" The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) replied: "Allāh and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will give testimony against every man and woman regarding what he or she did on its back. It will say: 'You committed such and such action on such and such day.' That is its news." (Tirmidhī)
408.commentary: We may commit sins thinking that we are alone, but Allāh (ﷻ) is Ever Watching and aware of all that we do. On the Day of Qiyāmah, the earth itself will testify against us. Allāh (ﷻ) will make objects such as the earth provide evidence for or against a person who committed good or bad deeds.

409.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "How can I enjoy life when the angel who has been deputed to blow the trumpet has already placed it in his mouth, with his ear turned in order to listen to the order to blow it so that he may blow it?" This statement weighed heavily on the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), so he said to them: "Say: 'Allāh is sufficient for us and an excellent guardian is He.'" (Tirmidhī)
409.commentary: Isrāfīl (عليه السلام) is the angel appointed to blow the trumpet at the end of the world, when every soul will die and Qiyāmah will take place. He is already poised with the trumpet in his mouth, awaiting the command from Allāh (ﷻ). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) instructed the Ṣaḥābah to say "ḥasbunā Allāh wa ni'ma al-wakīl" (Allāh is sufficient for us and an excellent guardian is He). This was the supplication of Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) when thrown into the fire.

410.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who fears departs in the first portion of the night and one who departs in the first portion of the night reaches his destination. Know that the commodity of Allāh is expensive. Know that the commodity of Allāh is Paradise." (Tirmidhī)
410.commentary: In this ḥadīth, a real life situation has been used to explain the importance of hastening towards good deeds. A traveller may be attacked by an enemy in the darkest hours of the night. One who fears such an attack will begin travelling early in the night, so that he can safely reach his destination. Similarly, our destination is the Hereafter, where we hope to live blissfully in Paradise. We must be courageous and hasten to perform good actions.

411.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "On the day of Qiyāmah, people will be raised bare-footed, naked and uncircumcised." I asked: "O Messenger of Allāh! Will all the men and women not be looking at each other?" He replied: "O 'Ā'ishah! The matter will be far too serious for them to be concerned with that." (Bukhārī, Muslim). Another narration has: "The matter will be far too serious for them to look at each other."
411.commentary: The ḥadīth indicates towards the severity and horror of the day of Qiyāmah and thereby encourages us to hasten towards repentance and good deeds. The horror of Qiyāmah will make all other matters seem trivial. On that day, people will flee from their near and dear ones and each person will be worried about the accounting of his own deeds. On the day of Qiyāmah, only certain elect people will have clothing.

412.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who testifies that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and that He is one and has no partner, that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, that 'Īsā is the servant of Allāh and His Messenger and His word which He cast into Maryam and a spirit from Him and that Paradise and the Hell-fire are true, then Allāh (ﷻ) shall enter him into Paradise no matter what his deeds may be." (Bukhārī, Muslim). Another narration of Muslim has: "Allāh (ﷻ) makes the Hell-fire unlawful for one who testifies that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh."
412.commentary: Aḥādīth such as this one serve to remind us that we should never lose hope in the endless mercy of Allāh (ﷻ). Once a person has accepted the fundamental beliefs of Islām, he will definitely enter Paradise if he dies in this condition. The statement "Allāh makes the Hell-fire unlawful for him" means that he will not be a permanent dweller of the Hell-fire. 'Īsā (عليه السلام) is given special mention because of the extreme beliefs held by the disbelievers about him.

413.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) says: 'One who does a good deed shall receive a reward ten times the like thereof, or I will give (him) more. One who commits an evil deed shall be punished the like thereof, or I will forgive (him). One who comes to Me by a hand-span, I go to him by a cubit. One who comes to Me by a cubit, I go to him by an arm-span. One who comes to Me walking, I go to him running. One who meets Me with sin equivalent to the size of the earth, but associated no partner with Me, I will meet him with a similar amount of forgiveness.'" (Muslim)
413.commentary: In this Ḥadīth al-Qudsī, Allāh (ﷻ) announces to His servants how He appreciates their eagerness for good deeds. We also learn about the intense magnitude of His mercy. When a servant performs a good deed, He multiplies the reward ten times or as much as He desires. But if the servant commits an act of disobedience, the punishment is not multiplied at all; rather, he will be punished in proportion to his misdeed, or Allāh (ﷻ) may even forgive him.

414.text: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Which two things are obligatory?" He replied: "One who dies without ascribing partners to Allāh (ﷻ) shall enter Paradise and one who dies ascribing partners to Allāh (ﷻ) shall enter the Hell-fire." (Muslim)
414.commentary: Paradise is guaranteed for a person who testifies to the tawḥīd (Oneness) of Allāh (ﷻ) and the prophethood of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and then fulfils the demands of that testimony, provided he dies in this state of īmān. To fulfil the demands of tawḥīd means to abstain from disobeying Allāh (ﷻ). If one had disobeyed Allāh, then he may first be punished in the Hell-fire before being admitted into Paradise. On the other hand, one who dies in a state of disbelief will be cast into the Hell-fire, to remain there forever.

415.text: One day the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was riding and Mu'ādh (رضي الله عنه) was sitting behind him. He said: "O Mu'ādh!" He replied: "O Messenger of Allāh! I am here and what a pleasure it is to be with you." He said: "O Mu'ādh!" He replied: "O Messenger of Allāh! I am here and what a pleasure it is to be with you." He said: "O Mu'ādh!" He replied: "O Messenger of Allāh! I am here and what a pleasure it is to be with you." This happened three times and he then said: "One who testifies sincerely from his heart, that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh, then Allāh (ﷻ) makes it unlawful for him to enter the Hell-fire." He said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Should I not convey this to the people so that they may rejoice?" He replied: "If you do so they will place their reliance on it." Anas (رضي الله عنه) said: "Mu'ādh (رضي الله عنه) narrated this at the time of his death, fearing the sin of concealing knowledge." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
415.commentary: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) repeatedly called Mu'ādh (رضي الله عنه) by name in order to get his full attention and emphasise the importance of what he was about to tell him. Mu'ādh (رضي الله عنه) desired to inform people of this ḥadīth, in order to give them joy and to encourage them towards sincerity in faith, but the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) wanted his Ummah to strive for the higher stages of the Hereafter by engaging in more acts of righteousness and he feared that if they learned of the ḥadīth they may suffice on this virtue and abandon other good deeds.

416.narrator: Abu Hurayrah or Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (ra)
416.text: Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) or Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī (رضي الله عنه) (the narrator is unsure, but such doubt with regard to a Ṣaḥābī is of no consequence because all the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) were completely reliable) said: "During the expedition of Tabūk, the people were suffering from hunger, so they said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! If you permit us, we will slaughter our camels, eat their meat and use the fat.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Alright, you may do so.' But 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) suggested: 'O Messenger of Allāh! If you do so, our conveyances will decrease. Rather ask them to bring their remaining provisions and supplicate to Allāh (ﷻ) so that He puts blessings in them. In this way Allāh (ﷻ) may place barakah (blessings) in their provisions.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Alright.' He then requested for a leather mat which he spread out and asked the people to bring their remaining provisions. Some brought a handful of grain, others a handful of dates and yet others a piece of bread, until a few things were gathered on the mat. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then supplicated for blessings and said to the people: 'Fill your utensils with this.' They began filling their utensils until every single utensil in the army was full. They ate until they were satiated and there was still some left over. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'I testify that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and that I am the Messenger of Allāh. One, who meets Allāh (ﷻ) with these two testimonies, without doubting them, will not be prevented from Paradise.'" (Muslim)
416.commentary: The battle of Tabūk was the last expedition (ghazwah) in which the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) personally took part. It was a long journey in extreme heat and provisions were scarce. When their rations began to run out, 'Umar (رضي الله عنه), who was an advisor to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), suggested that it would be better to gather the little food that they had and supplicate to Allāh (ﷻ) to grant barakah therein. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) accepted his suggestion and Allāh (ﷻ) accepted his du'ā' in their favour.

417.text: 'Itbān ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه), one of those who participated in the battle of Badr, narrates: "I used to lead my people, the Banū Sālim, in ṣalāh. When it used to rain a river of water would form between me and them making it difficult to reach their masjid. So I came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and said: 'My eyesight is weak and when it rains water flows in the valley between me and my people, making it difficult to cross. I would like you to come to my house and offer ṣalāh at a place which I will make into a place of ṣalāh.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) replied: 'I will come.' The following day when the sun was quite hot, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) came and the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sought permission to enter. I gave him permission to enter. He did not sit down and asked me: 'Where in your house would you like me to offer ṣalāh?' I indicated to the place where I preferred him to offer ṣalāh. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) stood and said the takbīr and we made a row and prayed behind him. He offered two rak'ats of ṣalāh and ended it with salām. We did the same. I then asked him to remain behind to eat khazīrah which had been prepared for him. When my neighbours heard that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was in my house, they began entering until many people were gathered. One of them asked: 'Where is Mālik? I do not see him?' Another replied: 'That man is a hypocrite. He does not love Allāh and His Messenger.' On hearing this, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Do not say that. Do you not see that he testifies that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and says it for the pleasure of Allāh?' The man said: 'Allāh and His Messenger know best. As far as we know, his inclinations and conversations are only with the hypocrites.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'One who testifies that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh, desiring thereby the pleasure of Allāh, then Allāh (ﷻ) makes it unlawful for him to enter the Hell-fire.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
417.commentary: It was a great honour for 'Itbān (رضي الله عنه) that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) entered his house and performed ṣalāh in it. When people began to speak ill of a Ṣaḥābī named Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum (رضي الله عنه) and accused him of being a hypocrite, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) declared him to be a true believer, on the basis that he had sincerely testified to the kalimah (testimony of faith) for the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ). Mālik (رضي الله عنه) was in fact part of the elite group of Ṣaḥābah who took part in the decisive battle of Badr.

418.text: Some prisoners were brought to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and a woman from among them was anxiously searching for her child. As soon as she found an infant among the prisoners, she took hold of it, clutched it to her belly and breast-fed it. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) addressed us saying: 'Do you think that this woman will ever cast her child into a fire?' We replied: 'No, by Allāh.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed Allāh (ﷻ) has far more mercy for His servants than this woman has for her child.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
418.commentary: This incident took place after the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims fought the Hawāzin tribe and took prisoners from amongst them. The woman had lost her child, and was frantically going around searching for her child. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) took advantage of the situation to teach the Ṣaḥābah a lesson. He explained that the mercy of Allāh (ﷻ) towards His servants is much more than the mercy of a mother for her child.

419.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When Allāh (ﷻ) created the creation, He wrote in a book which is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy overpowers My anger.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim). Another narration has: "(My mercy) overpowered My anger," and another narration has: "(My mercy) surpassed My anger."
419.commentary: Allāh's (ﷻ) decision to reward and benefit an obedient servant is termed as His pleasure and mercy, whereas the decision to punish and disgrace a disobedient servant is termed as His anger. Among the manifestations of Allāh's (ﷻ) mercy are that Allāh (ﷻ) equally provides sustenance for the obedient and the disobedient, He tolerates those who disbelieve in Him and who disobey Him and He accepts the repentance of those who repent to Him.

420.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Allāh (ﷻ) divided mercy into one hundred parts. He withheld ninety-nine parts for Himself and sent one part to the earth. It is through this one part that the creation shows mercy to each other, so that an animal lifts its hoof in fear of hurting its young one." Another narration has: "Allāh (ﷻ) has one hundred mercies. He sent down one mercy that is shared between jinn, men, animals and insects and by virtue of this they show affection and mercy to each other and a wild animal shows affection to its young. Allāh (ﷻ) withheld ninety-nine mercies and by virtue of these He will show mercy to His servants on the day of Qiyāmah." (Bukhārī, Muslim). Muslim also narrated from Salmān al-Fārsī (رضي الله عنه) that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) has one hundred mercies. One of these is the mercy by which the creation shows mercy to each other, while the other ninety-nine are for the day of Qiyāmah."
420.commentary: After mentioning that all creatures – jinn, humans, animals and insects – show mercy to one another, reference has been made to an animal with hooves such as a horse showing mercy to its foal. The reason for this is that horses were the most common domesticated animals for the Ṣaḥābah and they noticed how these animals behaved with their young. These narrations are a source of great hope and joy for a believer. Allāh (ﷻ) has already given him enormous bounties in this world, which include Islām, the Qur'ān, ṣalāh, etc. If all of this is the result of just one mercy, then one can well imagine the blessing of the ninety-nine mercies Allāh (ﷻ) will grant him in the Hereafter.

421.text: From the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) in what he narrates from Allāh (ﷻ) Who said: "A servant committed a sin and said: 'O Allāh! Forgive me my sin.' Allāh (ﷻ) said: 'My servant committed a sin, but he knows that he has a Sustainer who forgives sins and also punishes sins.' The servant again committed a sin and said: 'O my Sustainer! Forgive me my sin.' Allāh (ﷻ) said: 'My servant committed a sin, but he knows that he has a Sustainer who forgives sins and also punishes sins.' The person again committed a sin and said: 'O my Sustainer! Forgive me my sin.' Allāh (ﷻ) said: 'My servant committed a sin, but he knows that he has a Sustainer who forgives sins and also punishes sins. I have forgiven My servant, so he may now do as he likes.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim). The words "He may now do as he likes," mean that as long as he repents after sinning, Allāh (ﷻ) will forgive him because repentance wipes out previous sins.
421.commentary: This Ḥadīth al-Qudsī indicates the importance of promptly repenting after committing a sin. Such repentance should be genuine and not merely be words. It needs to be coupled with remorse over the sin, a firm commitment not to return to it and complete separation from it. When a person repents in this manner and asks Allāh (ﷻ) to forgive Him, Allāh (ﷻ) responds with His infinite quality of forgiveness. The ḥadīth does not mean that a person is allowed to commit as much evil as he likes. It means that if he happens to commit evil but also sincerely repents thereafter, then Allāh (ﷻ) will forgive him and he will once again have a clean slate.

422.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "I take an oath by that Being in whose control is my life that if you did not sin, Allāh (ﷻ) would have removed you and brought another nation which would commit sins and then seek Allāh's forgiveness so that He could forgive them." (Muslim)
422.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that Allāh (ﷻ) loves to forgive sin – a fact that we gather from other aḥādīth as well. No matter how much evil a person has perpetrated, he should never lose hope of the mercy and forgiveness of Allāh (ﷻ), for the door of tawbah (repentance) is wide open. He should hasten towards tawbah, knowing that he will be welcomed by Allāh (ﷻ). It is incorrect to assume from this ḥadīth that Islām encourages man to sin, because the Qur'ān repeatedly discourages sinning and the mission of the Messengers was to remove men from a life of sin.

423.narrator: Abū Ayyūb Khālid ibn Zayd (رضي الله عنه)
423.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "If you had not committed sins, Allāh (ﷻ) would have created other creatures which would commit sins and then seek forgiveness so that He could forgive them." (Muslim)
423.commentary: It is interesting to note that Abū Ayyūb (رضي الله عنه) only narrated this ḥadīth when he was on the verge of death. Many of the Ṣaḥābah and pious predecessors also narrated such aḥādīth of hope during their final moments of life. Ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه) said: "This ḥadīth is not an encouragement to commit sins; rather, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said this to console the Ṣaḥābah and remove excessive fear from their hearts. They had become so overwhelmed with fear that some of them had gone away to mountaintops to seclude themselves in worship, some of them had forsaken women and some had forsaken sleep. This ḥadīth directed them to develop hope in Allāh's (ﷻ) forgiveness."

424.text: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) together with Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) and 'Umar (رضي الله عنه). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then stood up and left us. After quite some time had passed and he still did not return, we began to fear that harm had come to him. We stood up in alarm. I was the first to be alarmed and I went out in search of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) until I reached an orchard belonging to the Anṣār." He then related the ḥadīth in full until he finally said: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Go and give glad tidings of Paradise to whoever you meet behind this orchard who testifies with full conviction of heart that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh (ﷻ).'" (Muslim)
424.commentary: Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) chose not to narrate the ḥadīth in full. From the narration quoted in Muslim, we learn that the Ṣaḥābah went out in search of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) reached an orchard belonging to the Banū al-Najjār clan of the Anṣār. He circled the orchard looking for a way in, but could not find any entrance. Finally, he noticed a brook flowing into the orchard through a gap beneath the walls. He squeezed through this opening and found the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) inside. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) gave him his sandals as an assurance that he was safe and sent him out with the glad tidings of Paradise for whoever testifies that there is none worthy of worship but Allāh (ﷻ) and that Muḥammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allāh.

425.narrator: Abdullāh ibn 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنهما)
425.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) recited the words of Allāh (ﷻ) regarding Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), "O my Sustainer! They have misguided many people. So whoever followed me, he is of me; and whoever disobeyed me, You are Most forgiving, Most merciful." (Sūrah Ibrāhīm, 36) and the words of 'Īsā (عليه السلام): "If You punish them, they are Your servants. And if You forgive them, You alone are powerful, wise." (Sūrah al-Mā'ida, 118) The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then raised his hands (in supplication) and said: "O Allāh! My followers, my followers," and he cried. Allāh (ﷻ) said: "O Jibra'īl! Go to Muḥammad and, despite your Lord knowing best, ask him why he is crying." Jibra'īl (عليه السلام) came to him and the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) informed him of his supplication, despite Allāh (ﷻ) knowing best. Allāh (ﷻ) then said: "O Jibra'īl! Go to Muḥammad and say: 'We will please you with regard to your followers and we will not displease you.'" (Muslim)
425.commentary: This ḥadīth illustrates the extreme compassion of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) for his Ummah and his concern for their well-being. When he recited the verses of the Qur'ān in which the Messengers Ibrāhīm and 'Īsā (عليهما السلام) supplicated to Allāh (ﷻ) for their respective followers, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) thought of his own followers and shed tears while supplicating for them. Allāh (ﷻ) consoled him and granted him what he desired with the assurance that He would please him with regard to his Ummah. Imām Nawawī (رحمه الله) said: "This ḥadīth is one of the most comforting of aḥādīth for this Ummah."

426.text: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on a donkey when he said to him: 'O Mu'ādh! Do you know what Allāh's (ﷻ) right is on His servants and the servants' right is on Allāh (ﷻ)?' I replied: 'Allāh and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Allāh's (ﷻ) right on His servants is that they should worship Him and not ascribe partners with Him. And the servants' right on Allāh (ﷻ) is that He does not punish anyone who does not ascribe partners with Him.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! Should I not grant people the glad tidings of this?' He replied: 'No, if you do so, they will rely on it (and abandon good deeds).'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
426.commentary: What does "the servants' right on Allāh (ﷻ)" mean when we know that nobody in reality has any right over Allāh (ﷻ), because Allāh (ﷻ) is not obliged to any of His creation? Imām Qurṭubī (رحمه الله) answered this by stating that it refers to the reward that Allāh (ﷻ) has promised, out of His kindness. Since Allāh (ﷻ) does not go against His promise, His servants can definitely expect to receive a reward and this has been referred to as a 'right'. We know from other aḥādīth that Allāh (ﷻ) may punish believers who committed sins, even though they did not ascribe partners to Allāh (ﷻ). Scholars have explained that the entrance of sinful believers in the Fire is not termed as 'adhāb (punishment), because 'adhāb means to inflict pain along with humiliation. A believer will only enter the Fire to become purified and eligible for Paradise.

427.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies that there is none worthy of worship except Allāh and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh. This is the meaning of the verse: 'Allāh strengthens the believers with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.'" (Sūrah Ibrāhīm, 27) (Bukhārī, Muslim)
427.commentary: After a person dies, the two angels Munkar and Nakīr will come to his grave and question him about his Lord, his religion and the Messenger that was sent to him. If he is a true Muslim, Allāh (ﷻ) will enable him to give the correct replies, while a disbeliever will not be able to do so.

428.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a disbeliever does a good deed, he receives sustenance in return for it in this world. As for a believer, Allāh (ﷻ) stores his good deeds for him in the Hereafter and also rewards him with sustenance in this world because of his obedience." Another narration has: "Allāh (ﷻ) does not wrong a believer for doing a good deed; he is given something for it in this world and rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for a disbeliever, he receives sustenance in this world for the good deeds which he did for Allāh so that when he reaches the Hereafter, he will have no good deeds for which he is to be rewarded." (Muslim)
428.commentary: Many disbelievers in this world perform actions of goodness such as giving charity, joining family ties and helping people, however, these do not take them closer to Allāh (ﷻ) because they lack the prerequisite of īmān (faith). Allāh (ﷻ) gives them a reward for these actions in this world by granting them more wealth or protecting them from harm, but they will not receive any reward in the Hereafter. A believer, on the other hand, is rewarded for his good deeds in both the worlds.

429.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The similitude of the five daily Ṣalāhs is like that of an abundantly flowing river at your door in which you bath five times a day." (Muslim)
429.commentary: This ḥadīth emphasises the importance of discharging the duty of ṣalāh and presents glad tidings to those who do so. Ṣalāh performed five times a day has been compared to bathing in a river and thereby cleansing oneself of dirt because, just as repeated bathing removes all physical dirt from the body, regular and correct performance of ṣalāh cleanses a person from sins. According to the general view, however, this refers to minor sins, as tawbah (repentance) is required for the forgiveness of major sins.

430.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "When a Muslim man passes away and forty people who do not ascribe partners with Allāh (ﷻ) attend his funeral prayer, Allāh (ﷻ) accepts their intercession in his favour." (Muslim)
430.commentary: The Janāzah Ṣalāh (funeral prayer) is a prayer in which forgiveness is sought on behalf of the deceased Muslim. If the number of those who perform the funeral prayer reaches forty, it is hoped that Allāh (ﷻ) will accept their supplication and forgive the deceased. According to some scholars, there is greater hope that Allāh (ﷻ) will accept intercession on behalf of the deceased, if more righteous people attend his funeral prayer.

431.text: We were about forty people with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) in a tent and he asked: 'Would you like to be a quarter of the inhabitants of Paradise?' We replied: 'Yes.' He asked: 'Would you like to be a third of the inhabitants of Paradise?' We replied: 'Yes.' He said: 'By that Being in whose control is the life of Muhammad, I hope that you will be half the inhabitants of Paradise. This is because only a Muslim soul shall enter Paradise. In comparison to the polytheists, you are like a strand of white hair on the skin of a black ox, or like a strand of black hair on the skin of a red ox.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
431.commentary: Another ḥadīth states that the inhabitants of Paradise will consist of 120 rows of people and 80 of these will be Muslims. This means that the Muslims will be two thirds of the inhabitants of Paradise. This variation in numbers between narrations is not a contradiction, but served as a glad tiding to please the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and his Ummah regarding Allāh's (ﷻ) tremendous mercy upon them.

432.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "On the day of Qiyāmah, Allāh (ﷻ) will hand over a Jew or Christian to every Muslim and say: 'This is your redemption from the Hell-fire.'" According to another narration, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A group of Muslims will be brought on the day of Qiyāmah with sins the size of mountains and Allāh (ﷻ) will forgive them all." (Muslim)
432.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that Allāh (ﷻ) will forgive the sins of the Muslims due to His mercy for them and He will punish the disbelievers in the same proportion because of their sin and disbelief. According to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz (رحمه الله) as well as Imām Shāfi'ī (رحمه الله), this ḥadīth is the most encouraging of aḥādīth for a Muslim considering its allusion that every Muslim will gain salvation from Hell.

433.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "On the day of Qiyāmah, a believer will be brought close to his Sustainer so that He may place him under His mercy and protection. He will then make him confess to his sins by asking him: 'Do you confess to such-and-such a sin? Do you confess to such-and-such a sin?' He will reply: 'O my Sustainer! I confess.' Allāh (ﷻ) will say: 'I concealed them for you in the world and I forgive you for them today,' and he will then be given his book of good deeds." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
433.commentary: This ḥadīth informs us of the tremendous mercy of Allāh (ﷻ) upon the believers on the day of Qiyāmah when Allāh (ﷻ) will obliterate their sins and forgive them. Allāh's (ﷻ) asking them to confess to their sins and then forgiving them is an allusion to the verse of the Qur'ān, "An easy reckoning will be taken from him." (Sūrah al-Inshiqāq, 8)

434.text: A man kissed a woman and came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and told him. Allāh (ﷻ) then revealed the verse: 'Establish ṣalāh at the two ends of the day and during portions of the night. Verily good deeds wipe out evil deeds.' (Sūrah Hūd, 114) The man asked: 'Is this for me only, O Messenger of Allāh?' He replied: 'It is for my entire Ummah.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
434.commentary: In this ḥadīth, mention is made of a Ṣaḥābī who committed a minor sin and then requested the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) to cleanse him of it by means of a punishment. It was not a major sin that required penal punishment, however the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) were such that they regarded even their minor sins as major sins and they were not content until they had been forgiven or purified of them. The Qur'ānic verse was then revealed stating that ṣalāh obliterates minor sins and that there was no need to execute any punishment or penalty.

435.text: A man came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! I committed a sin which necessitates punishment, so mete it out to me.' It was the time of ṣalāh, so he joined the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) in ṣalāh. When he had completed the ṣalāh, he said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! I committed a sin which necessitates punishment, so mete out to me the judgment of the Book of Allāh.' He (ﷺ) asked: 'Were you present with us in the ṣalāh?' He replied: 'Yes.' He (ﷺ) said: 'You have been forgiven.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim). The words "I committed a sin which necessitates punishment," refer to an ordinary sin that is punishable and does not refer to penal punishments of the Sharī'ah such as the punishment for committing adultery or consuming alcohol. These latter punishments do not fall off by offering ṣalāh nor is it permissible for the leader to ignore them.
435.commentary: According to some scholars, in order to conceal the sin from others the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) did not delve into and probe his declaration. The ḥadīth also teaches us that it is advisable for a person not to expose his own sins, just as Allāh (ﷻ) has not exposed them to others.

436.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) is pleased with a servant who eats a morsel of food and then praises Him for it, or drinks a drink of water and then praises Him for it." (Muslim)
436.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that it is meritorious for a person to praise Allāh (ﷻ) by saying Alḥamdulillāh, with every morsel and drink because by doing so he recalls Allāh's (ﷻ) kind bounties upon him. It is also a reminder not to commit sin and thereby displease the Being who provides sustenance.

437.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) extends His hand at night so that the sinner of the day may turn in repentance and He extends His hand during the day so that the sinner of the night may turn in repentance, until the sun rises from the west." (Muslim)
437.commentary: The "hand of Allāh" is one of those attributes of Allāh (ﷻ), which we believe in without questioning. Some scholars interpret it figuratively by saying that it refers to the acceptance of repentance. This ḥadīth encourages us to have hope in the mercy of Allāh (ﷻ) and to hasten towards repentance.

438.narrator: Abū Najīḥ 'Amr ibn 'Abasah al-Sulamī (رضي الله عنه)
438.text: During the days of ignorance, I believed that people were astray and they were not on the truth because they worshipped idols. Then I heard of a man in Makkah who was speaking of certain things. So I mounted my conveyance and went to him. It was the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) who was secretly conveying his message while his people openly opposed him. So I planned to meet him secretly and succeeded in meeting him in Makkah. I asked him: 'What are you?' He replied: 'I am a Messenger.' I asked: 'What is a Messenger?' He replied: 'Allāh (ﷻ) has sent me.' I asked: 'What did He send you with?' He replied: 'He has sent me with the task of maintaining ties of kinship, destroying idols and that Allāh (ﷻ) be accepted as One, without ascribing any partner to Him.' I asked: 'Who is with you in this?' He replied: 'A free man and a slave.' At that time, Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) and Bilāl (رضي الله عنه) were with him. I said: 'I would like to follow you.' He said: 'You will not be able to do so at present. Do you not see my position and the position of my people? Rather return to your people and when you hear that I have prevailed, then come to me.' So I returned to my people and the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went to Madīnah while I remained with them. I continued seeking news and enquiring from people when he reached Madīnah..." He said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! Inform me about ṣalāh.'" He said: "'Perform the morning [Fajr] Ṣalāh and then abstain from ṣalāh until the sun has risen to the height of a spear. This is because when the sun rises, it rises between the two horns of Shaiṭān and it is at this time that the unbelievers prostrate before it. Then you may perform ṣalāh because that ṣalāh is witnessed and attended [by angels], until the shadow is equal to the spear. Then abstain from ṣalāh because at that time Hell is ignited. When the shadow begins increasing, you may perform ṣalāh because that ṣalāh is witnessed and attended [by angels], until you perform the 'Aṣr Ṣalāh. Then abstain from ṣalāh until the sun sets, because it sets between the two horns of Shaiṭān and it is at this time that the unbelievers prostrate before it.'" "I said: 'O Messenger of Allāh! Tell me about ablution (wuḍū').' He said: 'There is no person among you who brings his ablution water, gargles his mouth, places water in his nose and blows it out without the sins of his face, mouth and nose falling away. Then when he washes his face as Allāh (ﷻ) ordered him, the sins of his face fall away with the water from the sides of his beard. Then when he washes his hands until his elbows, the sins of his hands fall off with the water from the tips of his fingers. Then when he passes his wet hands over his head, the sins of his head fall off with the water from the ends of his hair. Then when he washes his feet until his ankles, the sins of his feet fall off with the water from the tips of his toes. When he then stands up and performs ṣalāh, praises Allāh (ﷻ), glorifies Him, expresses His majesty in accordance with His status and devotes his heart to Allāh (ﷻ), then he relieves himself of his sins like the day his mother gave birth to him.'" (Muslim)
438.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us the great virtues of wuḍū' and ṣalāh when performed correctly. The mention of ties of kinship in the same breath with the Oneness of Allāh (ﷻ) illustrates its pivotal role in Islām. When the physical strength of the believers is weaker than that of the disbelievers, they should conceal their faith in order to avoid unnecessary losses. Ṣalāh should be performed with concentration and devotion.

439.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When Allāh (ﷻ) intends to show mercy upon a nation, He takes away their Messenger before them and He makes him a forerunner and a predecessor before them; and when He intends to destroy a nation, He punishes them while their Messenger is still alive. He destroys them while he is alive and watching and he is pleased by their destruction because they rejected him and disobeyed his command." (Muslim)
439.commentary: This ḥadīth served as solace and consolation for the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) because his people opposed and disobeyed him when he invited them to the truth of Islām. It was also an encouragement for the Muslims to continue following his message and teachings so that they could be united with him in the Hereafter. Equally, it served as a warning to the disbelievers to reform their ways for fear that Allāh (ﷻ) may punish them in this world as He did to the nations of Lūṭ, Ṣāliḥ and Nūḥ (عليهم السلام).

440.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) said: 'I treat My servant according to his expectations of Me. I am with him wherever he remembers Me.' By Allāh, Allāh (ﷻ) is more pleased with the repentance of His servant then one of you who finds his lost conveyance and possessions in a barren land. 'Whoever comes close to Me by one span, I go closer to him by one hand span. One who approaches Me by a hand span, I approach him by an arm-span. If he comes to Me walking, I go to him running." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
440.commentary: This ḥadīth encourages us to have hope in the mercy of Allāh (ﷻ) and to hasten towards repentance. According to Imām Qurṭubī (رحمه الله), "I treat My servant according to his expectations of Me" applies to du'ā', tawbah and istighfār. In other words, Allāh (ﷻ) will accept du'ā' and repentance if a person has the faith that Allāh (ﷻ) has accepted it. The ḥadīth also tells of Allāh's (ﷻ) great pleasure at his servant's turning to Him in repentance.

441.text: Three days before his demise, he heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "None of you should die without having good thoughts about Allāh (ﷻ)." (Muslim)
441.commentary: This ḥadīth encourages us to have hope of Allāh's (ﷻ) mercy and not to despair, especially at the time of death. Scholars mention that the quality of fear should be dominant in a believer when he is young and healthy, while hope should be dominant when he is old and nearing his death.

442.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Allāh (ﷻ) says: 'O son of Adam! I will forgive you as long as you continue supplicating to Me and having hope in Me and I will not mind. O son of Adam! I will forgive you even if your sins reach the height of the skies and you then seek forgiveness from Me and I will not mind. O son of Adam! If you come to Me with sins equivalent to the size of the earth and then you meet Me without having ascribed any partners with Me, I will come to you with the equivalent amount of forgiveness.'" (Tirmidhī)
442.commentary: This ḥadīth reminds us of the overwhelming mercy of Allāh (ﷻ). He forgives all sins except shirk (ascribing partners to Allāh (ﷻ)). Even if one has committed many sins, one should not feel despondent. One should turn to Allāh (ﷻ) in sincere repentance and Allāh (ﷻ) will forgive him. Once Sufyān al-Thawrī (رحمه الله) was ill and Ḥammād ibn Salamah (رحمه الله) visited him. Sufyān al-Thawrī (رحمه الله) asked him, "Do you think that Allāh will forgive a person like myself?" Ḥammād (رحمه الله) replied, "If I had the choice of going to my father for accountability or to Allāh, I would choose Allāh because He is more merciful than a father."

443.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If a believer knew of the punishment of Allāh (ﷻ), he would have no hope of attaining His Paradise; and if a disbeliever knew of the mercy of Allāh (ﷻ), he would not despair of attaining His Paradise." (Muslim)
443.commentary: In this ḥadīth, we are warned of the severity of Allāh's (ﷻ) punishment so that we may be careful to avoid it and we are told of Allāh's (ﷻ) tremendous mercy so that we may remain hopeful of salvation. According to 'Allāmah Ṭībī (رحمه الله), this ḥadīth combines both of Allāh's (ﷻ) qualities of being the Almighty and the Merciful.

444.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When the corpse is laid out and people or men carry it on their shoulders, if it was righteous, it says: 'Take me forward, take me forward,' and if it was not righteous, it says: 'Destruction to me! Where are you taking it?' Everything except man hears its voice. If he were to hear it, he would fall unconscious." (Bukhārī)
444.commentary: If the deceased was righteous, he will be anxious to proceed to his grave in anticipation of the reward that Allāh (ﷻ) has prepared for him and if he was not, he will be afraid to enter his grave. According to some scholars, everything with the faculty of perception, except man, hears the soul of the deceased when it speaks. It is Sunnah to hasten with the burial of the deceased.

445.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Paradise is closer to you than your sandal straps and the Hell-fire is just the same." (Bukhārī)
445.commentary: Ibn Jawzī (رحمه الله) stated that this ḥadīth means that Paradise can be easily acquired with īmān and obedience to Allāh (ﷻ); similarly, Hell can be easily acquired by following the base desires and sinning. The ḥadīth also teaches us that we should not avoid doing any good deed, no matter how insignificant it may be, because we do not know whether Allāh's (ﷻ) pleasure lies therein. Similarly, we should not indulge in any sin, no matter how insignificant it may be, because we do not know whether Allāh's (ﷻ) anger lies therein.

446.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite the Qur'ān to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Should I recite the Qur'ān to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "I love to hear it from someone other than myself." So I recited Sūrah al-Nisā' to him, until I reached this verse: 'How will it be when We shall bring forth a witness from every nation and call you to be a witness over them?' (Sūrah al-Nisā', 41) He said: "That is sufficient for now." When I turned towards him, his eyes were flowing with tears." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
446.commentary: This ḥadīth encourages us to weep out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) when hearing His word, the Qur'ān. According to the scholars, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) cried due to his mercy and concern for his Ummah because he realized that he would need to testify regarding their actions, some of which would not be good and would lead to their punishment. It is also possible that he cried because he pictured the difficult scene of Qiyāmah when he would be called to intercede on behalf of his Ummah.

447.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) addressed us in a sermon the like of which I never heard before. He said: 'If you only knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much.' As a result, the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) covered their faces and wept." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
447.commentary: This ḥadīth was discussed in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 401. It teaches us that the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) wept when they heard advices encouraging the fear of Allāh (ﷻ). It encourages us to do likewise or at least to adopt the appearance of a weeping person when listening to the words of the Qur'ān or advices of the righteous.

448.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A person who cries out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) will not enter the Hell-fire until milk returns to the udders. Dust raised up in the path of Allāh (ﷻ) and the smoke of the Hell-fire can never combine." (Tirmidhī)
448.commentary: Rasūlullāh (ﷺ) utilised the example of milk returning to the udder in order to illustrate the impossibility of a person who cries out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) entering the Hell-fire. The Qur'ān utilises a similar example to explain an impossibility, "They will not enter Paradise until a camel enters through the eye of a needle." (Sūrah al-A'rāf, 40) The second portion of the ḥadīth states that the dust which covers the body while in the path of Allāh (ﷻ) and the smoke of the Hell-fire are opposites and can never be joined together.

449.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "There are seven people to whom Allāh (ﷻ) will provide shade beneath His shade on a day when there will be no shade except His shade: a just leader, a youth who grew up in the worship of Allāh (ﷻ), a person whose heart is attached to the masājid, two people who love each other for the sake of Allāh (ﷻ), meeting and parting ways only for the love of Allāh (ﷻ), a man who says to a woman of nobility and beauty trying to seduce him, 'I fear Allāh', a person who gives in charity and conceals it so that even his left hand does not know what his right hand gives, and a person who engages in the remembrance of Allāh (ﷻ) in solitude, while shedding tears." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
449.commentary: This ḥadīth has been comprehensively discussed in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 376. It is relevant to this chapter because it teaches us the virtue of a person who worships and remembers Allāh (ﷻ) in solitude and weeps because of His fear. Such fear and weeping will be a source of reward for him in the Hereafter.

450.text: I came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) while he was offering ṣalāh and his chest was emitting a sound like that of a kettle of boiling water because of his weeping." (Abū Dāwūd)
450.commentary: This ḥadīth describes the intensity of the worship of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). His fear of Allāh (ﷻ) and his superior level of obedience led him to weep and express his utter weakness before his Sustainer. Scholars say that the quality of weeping out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) was so dominant in Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) that he could be heard weeping from a distance of one mile.

451.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه): "Allāh (ﷻ) ordered me to recite [Sūrah] Lam yakunilladhīna... to you." He asked: "Did Allāh (ﷻ) mention me by name?" He (ﷺ) replied: "Yes," and Ubayy (رضي الله عنه) wept. (Bukhārī, Muslim)
451.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه) wept out of joy for Allāh's (ﷻ) command instructing the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) to recite the Qur'ān to him. It teaches us that to express joy by tearing when receiving a bounty from Allāh (ﷻ) is completely acceptable, as is weeping because of the realisation that one will never be able to be sufficiently grateful to Allāh (ﷻ) for that bounty. Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه) was the greatest reciter of the Qur'ān amongst the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم).

452.text: After the demise of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) said to 'Umar (رضي الله عنه): "Let us visit Umm Ayman (رضي الله عنها) as the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to visit her." When they went to her, she began crying, so they asked her: "Why are you crying? Don't you know that that which is with Allāh is better for the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)?" She replied: "I am not crying because I do not know that that which is with Allāh is better for the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ); rather, I am crying because divine revelation has now come to an end." This prompted them to cry as well and they began to cry with her. (Muslim)
452.commentary: This ḥadīth was discussed in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 360. It teaches us that it is permissible to shed tears upon the separation and demise of the pious and that this does not contradict the teaching to be content with the decisions of Allāh (ﷻ).

453.text: When the illness of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) became intense, he was asked about ṣalāh and he said: 'Order Abū Bakr to lead the people in ṣalāh.' 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) said: 'Abū Bakr is a soft-hearted person. When he recites the Qur'ān, he is overcome by weeping.' He (ﷺ) said: 'Order him to lead the ṣalāh.'" Another narration from 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) states that she said: "If Abū Bakr stands in your place, people will not hear his recitation because of his crying." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
453.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that weeping while reciting the Qur'ān is a meritorious deed. The ḥadīth also proves that Abū Bakr (رضي الله عنه) was the most eligible for the khilāfah after the demise of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allāh's (ﷺ) instruction for him to lead the ṣalāh was an indication that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) regarded him as the best of all the Ṣaḥābah. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said, "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) chose him for our religious matters. Why should we not prefer him for our worldly matters?"

454.text: Food was brought to 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf (رضي الله عنه) [my father] while he was fasting and he said: "Muṣ'ab ibn 'Umayr (رضي الله عنه) was killed and he was better than me. Nothing could be found to enshroud him except a sheet, which was such that if his head was covered with it, his feet were exposed and if his feet were covered with it, his head was exposed. Then there came a time when the treasures of the world were laid out before us," - or he said: "We have now been given so much of the world." - "and we fear that the rewards for our good deeds have been given to us in advance." He then began weeping to such an extent that he left the food. (Bukhārī)
454.commentary: This ḥadīth explains that the noble Ṣaḥābī, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf (رضي الله عنه), was of the opinion that the treasures of the world which were given to them was the reward for their good deeds and that they would therefore not receive any reward in the Hereafter. This showed his concern for success in the Hereafter. It is advisable to mention the bounties of Allāh (ﷻ) that one enjoys, so that one may be grateful for them and express ones inability to appreciate them fully. Humility is a virtue. Despite 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf (رضي الله عنه) being one of the 'Asharah Mubassharah (the ten Ṣaḥābah who were promised Paradise), he regarded Muṣ'ab ibn 'Umayr (رضي الله عنه) to be more virtuous than himself.

455.narrator: Abū Umāmah Ṣudayy ibn 'Ajlān al-Bāhilī (رضي الله عنه)
455.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "There is nothing which Allāh (ﷻ) loves more than two drops and two signs: a teardrop that is shed out of the fear of Allāh (ﷻ) and a drop of blood that is shed in the path of Allāh (ﷻ). As for the two signs, one is a sign left in the path of Allāh (ﷻ) and the other is a sign when fulfilling one of the compulsory duties of Allāh (ﷻ)." (Tirmidhī)
455.commentary: From this ḥadīth, we learn that Allāh (ﷻ) loves two drops of fluid. One is that teardrop which falls from the eye of a person due to His fear and the other is that drop of blood that falls from the body of a mujāhid who is injured in His path. We also learn that Allāh (ﷻ) loves two signs and effects. One is that footstep taken or injury incurred in the path of Allāh (ﷻ). The other is the effect that remains on the body due to an act of worship, such as cracks on the feet due to wuḍū' in the cold, a dusty body during ḥaj, the effects of ṣalāh on the forehead and weakness as a result of ṣawm or ṣalāh.

456.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) addressed us in a sermon which made our hearts tremble and our eyes tear." (Refer to ḥadīth no. 157)
456.commentary: This ḥadīth was discussed in a previous chapter. The full narration appears in ḥadīth 157. It teaches us the great effect that the sermons and advices of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had on the Ṣaḥābah, causing their hearts to tremble and their eyes to shed tears.

457.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sent Abū 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (رضي الله عنه) to Bahrain in order to collect its jizyah. He returned with the wealth from Bahrain and when the Anṣār heard about the arrival of Abū 'Ubaydah (رضي الله عنه), they arrived to offer the Fajr Ṣalāh with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) completed the ṣalāh, he turned around to leave, but the Anṣār presented themselves before him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) smiled when he saw them and said: 'I assume that you heard of Abū 'Ubaydah's arrival with something from Bahrain?' They replied: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allāh.' He said: 'Glad tidings be to you and hope for that which will make you happy. By Allāh, I do not fear poverty for you, but I fear that the world be laid out before you as it was laid out for those before you and you will compete for it as they competed for it and it will destroy you as it destroyed them.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
457.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that wealth, luxuries and competition in worldly possessions often lead a person to commit sin and transgression. One therefore, should strive to cleanse the heart of the love of this world. The ḥadīth serves as a warning to those who are wealthy because wealth brings power and power easily corrupts noble intentions. The Ṣaḥābah were poor, but because they went out in jihād, the wealth of the world came to them and they enjoyed honour and dignity amongst humanity. In contrast, the later generations were wealthy, but because they abandoned their religious responsibilities, they lost what they had and were disgraced amongst humanity.

458.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sat on the pulpit and we sat around him. He said: "Part of what I really fear for you after my demise is that the beauty and splendour of the world will be opened up to you." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
458.commentary: The ḥadīth explains that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) feared that the hearts and minds of Muslims would be drawn to the attractions of the world resulting in indifference towards the Hereafter. He feared that they would neglect their primary religious responsibilities of jihād and propagating Islām. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was well aware that love for wealth and riches creates enmity, pride and miserliness.

459.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The world is sweet and green and Allāh (ﷻ) has made you vicegerents therein in order to observe what you do. So be wary of the world and be wary of women." (Muslim)
459.commentary: This ḥadīth was discussed in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 70. This world has been referred to as sweet and green because of its attraction to man. It also indicates to its temporary and perishable nature. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) advised that one should "be wary of the world" because its attractions lead one astray from the straight path. One should also "be wary of women" because one who becomes engrossed with them is easily distracted from fulfilling his religious obligations.

460.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "O Allāh! There is no life except the life of the Hereafter." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
460.commentary: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said these words on the most difficult of occasions and on the happiest of occasions. The former was when the Ṣaḥābah were strenuously digging the trench around Madīnah Munawwarah and he consoled them by saying that their exertion and toils were nothing compared to the everlasting pleasure of the Hereafter. The latter was when a great multitude of Ṣaḥābah performed the Farewell Ḥaj and he cautioned them that they should not develop pride because of their numbers and physical strength, but remain focused on the true life of the Hereafter. The essence of his message was that the ease and luxuries of this world do not please an intelligent person because these are transient, rather his focus should be the Hereafter which is eternal.

461.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Three things follow the deceased: his family, his wealth and his actions. Two of them return and one remains with him. His family and wealth return and his actions remain with him." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
461.commentary: This ḥadīth encourages a person to engage in good actions in the world because only these will benefit him in his grave and in the Hereafter.

462.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "An inmate of Hell who had been from the wealthiest of people in this world will be brought on the day of Qiyāmah and dipped into the Hell-fire. He will then be asked: 'O son of Adam! Did you ever experience any good? Did you ever experience any blessing?' He will say: 'By Allāh, no, my Sustainer.' And an inmate of Paradise who had suffered the most in this world will be brought and dipped into Paradise. He will then be asked: 'O son of Adam! Did you ever experience any suffering? Did any difficulty ever afflict you?' He will say: 'By Allāh, no, my Sustainer. I never experienced any suffering nor did any difficulty ever afflict me.'" (Muslim)
462.commentary: The ḥadīth explains that a disbeliever will be dipped very briefly into hell and it will cause him to forget every bounty, which he had enjoyed in this world. His reply that he had never experienced any bounties in this world is an indication of the severity of hell. It is as if all the bounties of the world were nothing compared to the brief punishment of hell. On the other hand, a person who had suffered much in this world will be dipped very briefly into Paradise and it will cause him to forget every difficulty and hardship he experienced in this world. In other words, a person who gets just one taste of Paradise will be so overawed by its bounties that he will regard all his suffering in this world as nothing.

463.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "This world in comparison to the Hereafter is like dipping your finger in the sea and seeing how much water sticks to it." (Muslim)
463.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that the quantity of water, which sticks onto ones finger when it is dipped into the sea is like this world, while the entire sea is like the Hereafter. In other words, the insignificance and transient nature of this world is being compared to the countless bounties and eternity of the Hereafter. It is to be noted that this is merely an example that has been mentioned so that man may understand the difference between this world and the Hereafter. In reality, there can be no comparison because one is temporary and the other is eternal.

464.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed through the market place with people on either side of him. He passed by the dead kid of a goat which had small ears. He held it by its ear and asked: "Which of you would like to purchase this for one dirham?" The Ṣaḥābah replied: "We would not like to take it for anything. What could we do with it?" He asked: "Would you like to have it?" They replied: "By Allāh, even if it was alive, it would have been defective because of its small ears. How can we like it now that it is dead!" He said: "By Allāh, this world is more insignificant in the sight of Allāh (ﷻ) than this kid is to you." (Muslim)
464.commentary: In various ways and on many occasions, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) discouraged the Ṣaḥābah from becoming submerged in the love of this world because this causes a person to desire more of it and commit sins without any fear of Allāh (ﷻ). The Messengers, scholars, the righteous, the divine books and all forms of worship are excluded from the description of the world being insignificant and worthless.

465.text: I was walking with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on a lava field of Madīnah with Mount Uḥud in front of us. He (ﷺ) said: 'O Abū Dharr!' I replied: 'I am present, O Messenger of Allāh!' He said: 'It would not please me to have gold equal to this mountain of Uḥud and three days pass by with even a single dīnār of it remaining with me, except an amount with which I could pay off debts. Rather, I would distribute it among the servants of Allāh (ﷻ) like this, like this and like this,' and he indicated to his right, his left and behind him. He continued walking and then said: 'Those who have a lot of wealth (in this world) will have very little (in reward) on the day of Qiyāmah, except for the person who distributes his wealth like this, like this and like this,' and he indicated to his right, his left and behind him." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
465.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us not to develop love for this temporary world, and to rather spend our wealth in the path of Allāh (ﷻ). 'Īsā (عليه السلام) appropriately stated, "Do not make the world your master because it will make you its slave." It should be noted that the ḥadīth does not imply that to be wealthy is forbidden. It simply means that one should fulfil the rights of the wealth that Allāh (ﷻ) bestows upon a person. It is permissible for a person to save money for an unseen expense; however, one should not be miserly or wasteful.

466.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If I had gold equal to Mount Uḥud, it would not please me that any of it remains with me for three days, except an amount with which I could pay off debts." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
466.commentary: This ḥadīth indicates towards the ultimate degree of abstinence of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ); he would not even allow three days to pass with excess wealth in his possession. Paying off a debt is Farḍ (obligatory) while charity is Nafl (optional); hence, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) gave preference to the settling of debts and kept sufficient wealth for this purpose. One should spend in the path of Allāh (ﷻ) during one's lifetime while one is healthy, rather than at the time of death. One should hasten in settling one's debts. A wealthy person who delays in settling debts commits oppression.

467.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Look at those who are below you and do not look at those who are above you. That will be more likely to prevent you from being ungrateful for Allāh's bounties on you." (Bukhārī, Muslim) The narration of Bukhārī has: "When any of you sees someone who has been given more than him in wealth and physical appearance, he should look at someone who is below him."
467.commentary: This ḥadīth provides a prescription for contentment and peace. One should look towards the less fortunate in worldly terms to appreciate one's bounties and be grateful to Allāh. Looking towards those who are wealthy leads to envy and jealousy. In matters of religion and the Hereafter, one should look towards those who are superior so that one may strive to equal them in righteousness.

468.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "May the slave of the dīnār, the dirham, the velvet cloak and the silk garment be destroyed. If he is given, he is pleased and if he is not given, he is displeased." (Bukhārī)
468.commentary: This ḥadīth discourages us from developing excessive love for this world and its luxuries because one who is a slave to wealth cannot be a true slave to Allāh. One who becomes engrossed in the wealth of this world to the extent that he gives preference to it over religion, becomes a slave to it and worships it instead of worshipping Allāh.

469.text: I saw seventy people of the people of the Ṣuffah and not a single man among them had a cloak. They had either a loincloth or an upper garment, which they tied around their necks. Some of these garments reached their calves, while others reached their ankles. They would gather it with their hands fearing that their private parts would be exposed." (Bukhārī)
469.commentary: The Ṣuffah was a raised platform in Masjid al-Nabawī on which the poverty stricken Ṣaḥābah would reside in order to learn Islām from the Messenger of Allāh. This ḥadīth highlights the poverty of the Ṣaḥābah of the Ṣuffah; they barely had sufficient clothing to cover their bodies. They chose a life of simplicity and suppressed their desires in order to learn the religion of Islām and benefit from it in the Hereafter.

470.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The world is a prison for the believer and a Paradise for the disbeliever." (Muslim)
470.commentary: This ḥadīth can be interpreted in various ways: No matter how much luxury a believer has in this world, it is minimal compared to that of the Hereafter; and no matter how severely a disbeliever suffers in this world, it is minimal compared to what punishment awaits him in the Hereafter. Also, just as a prisoner is confined and restricted in his movements and actions, a believer is restricted by the commands of Allāh. In contrast, a disbeliever is free to do as he pleases.

471.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) took hold of my shoulders and said: 'Live in this world as if you are a stranger or one who is travelling on a path.' Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما) used to say: 'In the evening, do not expect to see the morning and in the morning, do not expect to see the evening. Prepare for your illness while you are healthy and prepare for your death while you are living.'" (Bukhārī)
471.commentary: The ḥadīth imparts various lessons such as to hasten towards good deeds, abandon long-drawn aspirations, capitalize on opportunities, avoid procrastination, utilize the bounties of life and wealth in a spiritually beneficial manner, be content with little and be prepared for death at any time. The ḥadīth teaches us to prepare for the Hereafter, which is eternal and not to expand all our energies for this transient world.

472.narrator: Abū al-'Abbās Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sā'idī (رضي الله عنه)
472.text: A man came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Show me an action which, if I engage in, Allāh (ﷻ) will love me and the people will love me." He said: "Make do with little of this world and Allāh (ﷻ) will love you and make do with little of what people own and people will love you." (ibn Mājah)
472.commentary: The ḥadīth discourages a person from being engrossed in this world to the extent that its love enters his heart. Love of the world is despised from an Islāmic perspective; however, one who loves the world in order to worship Allāh, do good deeds and assist the creation is not discouraged, but rewarded. The ḥadīth also encourages contentment and discourages a person from asking of people.

473.text: What people had acquired of this world and then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) spending the day twisting and turning due to hunger; he could not even find poor quality dates to fill his stomach." (Muslim)
473.commentary: This ḥadīth and many others depict the sacrifice of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and his focus upon the Hereafter. Other narrations teach us that the prophetic household would often spend nights without a meal.

474.text: When the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed away there was nothing in my house which any living creature could eat, except a little barley which was stored on a shelf. I continued eating from it for quite some time, but then I weighed it and it got finished." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
474.commentary: Despite the large amounts of booty that arrived in Madīnah Munawwarah during the final stages of the life of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), he chose to live a life of simplicity and poverty. In other words, wealth did not corrupt the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) or change the way he lived in this world. This was the excellent example of leadership he set for humanity to emulate.

475.text: 'Amr ibn al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنه), the brother of Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنها), the mother of the believers, narrates: "At the time of the demise of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), he did not leave behind any dīnār, dirham, male slave, female slave, nor anything other than his white mule which he used to ride, his weapons and a portion of land which he had given in charity for travellers." (Bukhārī)
475.commentary: This ḥadīth mentions that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) left behind almost no possessions at the time of his demise. The land referred to here is that of Fadak, Khaibar and a portion of the land of Banū Nadhīr. The latter was obtained after the battle of Uḥud, but the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) distributed it thereafter. The land of Fadak was made waqf for travellers and he divided the land of Khaibar into three portions: two thirds were for the benefit of the Muslims, while the remaining third was for the benefit of the wives of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ).

476.text: We emigrated with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), seeking the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ). Allāh (ﷻ) granted us our reward; some of us died without enjoying any of their reward and Muṣ'ab ibn 'Umayr (رضي الله عنه) was one of them. He was killed in the battle of Uḥud and left behind a shawl. When we covered his head with it, his feet became exposed and when we covered his feet with it, his head became exposed. So the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) commanded us to cover his head and to place some grass on his feet. Some of us are picking the fruits which have ripened." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
476.commentary: This ḥadīth illustrates the simplicity and truthfulness of the Ṣaḥābah. They sincerely fought alongside the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) for the pleasure of Allāh and not for any worldly motives. Some of them did not even have a burial shroud that could cover their bodies. The ḥadīth also teaches us that those righteous servants of Allāh who victoriously return from battle receive the worldly rewards of their efforts in the form of booty, as well as an eternal reward. Those who are blessed with martyrdom will receive their full reward in the Hereafter.

477.narrator: Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sā'idī (رضي الله عنه)
477.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If the world had been worth as much as the wing of a mosquito in the sight of Allāh (ﷻ), He would not have given a single sip of water to a disbeliever." (Tirmidhī)
477.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that the world has no real worth because Allāh has given it to His enemies, the disbelievers and it is obvious that an enemy is never given an item of value as a gift. A mosquito is regarded as an insignificant and trivial creature and this world should be regarded in the same way. Allāh has not created the world as the ultimate objective of life; rather, it is to be used as a means of achieving the greater objective, which is the Hereafter.

478.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Listen! This world is cursed and all that is in it is cursed, except the remembrance of Allāh (ﷻ), whatever is beloved to Him, an Islāmic scholar and a student." (Tirmidhī)
