1724.commentary: Allāh loves humility and simplicity and dislikes boastfulness and arrogance. One who calls himself 'the king of kings' displays arrogance, hence it is forbidden for any man to utilise this title.

1725.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not address a hypocrite as 'master'. Even if he is a master, you would have angered your Sustainer." (Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1725.commentary: The word 'master' is a title of honour and should not be used to address a hypocrite because he is never worthy of honour and respect. A hypocrite is an enemy of Allāh and should therefore not be praised. Just as light and darkness cannot combine, the heart of a believer cannot combine the love for Allāh and the love for the enemy of Allāh. Scholars state that a disbeliever, misguided individual, flagrant sinner and innovator should similarly not be addressed in respectful terms. It is unfortunate that nowadays, disbelieving sports players, musicians and actors are passionately praised and respected.

1726.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went to Umm al-Sā'ib – or Umm al-Musayyab – and said: 'O Umm al-Sā'ib – or Umm al-Musayyab – what is wrong, why are you trembling?' She replied: 'It is because of my fever. May Allāh not bless it!' He said: 'Do not curse the fever because it removes the sins of man just as the bellows remove the filth of iron.'" (Muslim, Bayhaqī)
1726.commentary: Sickness is a blessing for a believer because it obliterates his sins. By cursing or speaking evil of it, one does not appreciate this bounty and further expresses displeasure for Allāh's decision. One should rather accept it as Allāh's decree and part of fate. It does not mean that one should not seek a cure for it because seeking a cure is Sunnah and encouraged in Islām.

1727.narrator: Abū al-Mundhir Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه)
1727.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not curse the wind. If you dislike anything of it, say: 'O Allāh, we ask You for the good of this wind, the good that it contains, and the good which it has been commanded to do. We seek refuge in You from the evil of this wind, the evil that it contains, and the evil which it has been commanded to do." (Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1727.commentary: The blowing of the wind is a mercy and bounty of Allāh because it brings clouds of rain and it enables ships to sail on the oceans. For these reasons, a believer should not curse it or speak evil of it. He should rather supplicate to Allāh to bring goodness with it. At times, Allāh utilises the wind to punish those who are transgressors and sinners, such as the nation of 'Ād, however the scholars have mentioned that this is also a bounty because it purifies the earth of sinners without harming those who are obedient to Allāh.

1728.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "The wind is from the mercy of Allāh. It brings mercy and punishment. When you see it, do not curse it. Ask Allāh for the good of it and seek refuge in Him from the evil of it." (Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1728.commentary: One should never curse the creations of Allāh because they are all subservient to His will. A believer should focus towards Allāh in supplication when witnessing any difficulty or calamity.

1729.text: When the wind would blow strongly, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say: 'O Allāh, I ask You for the good of it, the good that it contains, and the good which it has been sent with. I seek refuge in You from the evil of it, the evil that it contains, and the evil which it has been sent with.'" (Muslim)
1729.commentary: This du'ā' should be recited when strong winds blow.

1730.narrator: Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī (رضي الله عنه)
1730.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not curse the rooster because it awakens the people for ṣalāh." (Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1730.commentary: That the crowing of a rooster disrupts the pleasure of sleep should not cause one to speak evil of it because the ṣalāh towards which it calls is far superior. Some scholars are of the opinion that the ṣalāh referred to here is Tahajjud as a narration states that the Messenger used to awake for Tahajjud when the rooster crowed. Other scholars state that it refers to Fajr ṣalāh. The fact that we have been commanded not to speak evil of an animal which benefits mankind, teaches us that a believer should be respected all the more because he is of greater benefit to mankind.

1731.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) led us in the Fajr ṣalāh at Ḥudaybiyah, after some rain had fallen during the night. When he completed the ṣalāh, he turned towards the people and said: 'Do you know what your Sustainer has said?' The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) replied: 'Allāh and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Allāh said: 'This morning some of My servants are believers and others are disbelievers. Those who said, 'We had rain by the grace and mercy of Allāh', believe in Me and disbelieve in the stars. Those who said, 'We had rain on account of so-and-so star', disbelieve in Me, but believe in the stars.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1731.commentary: To attribute the falling of rain to any being or creation other than Allāh is shirk (polytheism) and a denial of Allāh as the supreme controller. Allāh is in complete control of the rains as the Qur'ān states, "It is He who sends the rain after people have lost hope." (Sūrah al-Shūrā, 28) Hence, we believe and accept that no entity or being besides Allāh sends rain, causes vegetation to grow or provides sustenance.

1732.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a person says to his brother: 'O disbeliever,' one of the two returns with that designation. He is either eligible for it or it returns to him." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1732.commentary: The ḥadīth means that incorrectly labelling a believer as a disbeliever will cause the person who made the designation to become a disbeliever if he considered his designation as permissible, because he regarded īmān as disbelief. It could also mean that his words do not harm the believer, but will result in him committing an act of disbelief.

1733.text: He heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "One who addresses another as a disbeliever or says to him: 'O enemy of Allāh,' when that is not the case, it reverts to him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1733.commentary: A Muslim can only be called a disbeliever if he unambiguously and explicitly utters a statement of disbelief such as denying a fundamental of Islām as established in the Qur'ān. Based on this ḥadīth, one should be especially cautious of referring to another Muslim as a disbeliever or enemy of Allāh because there is a possibility that if his designation is false, it will be to his own detriment.

1734.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A believer is not one who insults, curses, and utters obscene and immoral speech." (Tirmidhī)
1734.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 1555. It stresses upon the importance of guarding the tongue from immoral speech. It also teaches us that a believer is one whose character is noble and not obscene and offensive.

1735.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Immodesty is not found in anything without spoiling it and modesty is not found in anything without beautifying it." (Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, Aḥmad)
1735.commentary: Vulgarity and unnecessary harshness are the ingredients of an evil personality while gentleness and kindness generate honour and respect.

1736.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Those who exaggerate are destroyed." He said this three times. (Muslim)
1736.commentary: Allāh dislikes a person who goes to great lengths in attempting to speak eloquently. Scholars state that simple and sincere words have an impact upon the hearts of the audience, while eloquent words may stir people's emotions but in reality fail to impact upon the heart. These aḥādīth also imply that one should not speak to an audience beyond their level of comprehension because it will cause unnecessary confusion in their minds.

1737.narrator: Abdullāh ibn 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه)
1737.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh detests a person who exaggerates in speaking eloquently by rolling out his tongue like a cow." (Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1737.commentary: Allāh dislikes a person who goes to great lengths in attempting to speak eloquently.

1738.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The most beloved of you to me and those of you who will be seated closest to me on the day of Qiyāmah will be those of you who have the best character. The most detested of you to me and those of you who will be furthest away from me on the day of Qiyāmah will be those who talk excessively, who brag when talking, and who adopt an arrogant manner in speech in order to display their superiority." (Tirmidhī, Aḥmad)
1738.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 631. It stresses that noble character constitutes speaking in a humble and simple manner. One should not attempt to display one's eloquence or stamp one's authority over others when speaking because this is a reflection of pride.

1739.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "None of you should say: 'I am feeling disgusted.' He should rather say: 'I am feeling annoyed.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1739.commentary: Both these words have a similar meaning, however we have been instructed to utilise the one which does not denote an undesirable meaning. Some scholars state that the reason for this discouragement is that Allāh has created man in honour and he should therefore not degrade himself. 'Allāmah Khaṭṭābī stated that Islām has gone to the extent of teaching us the manner of giving expression to our words. We should utilise positive words and expressions instead of negative ones.

1740.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not refer to grapes as 'al-karm' because a Muslim is 'al-karm'." Another narration has: "Al-karm is the heart of a believer." A narration of Bukhārī and Muslim has: "People say al-karm whereas al-karm is the heart of a believer." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1740.commentary: During the days of ignorance, the pagan Arabs used to squeeze wine from grapes and they believed that when a person drank it he would develop qualities of generosity, kindness and bravery. When Islām forbade alcohol, it discouraged naming grapes and wine as al-karm because believing that wine develops these qualities in a person is incorrect. In addition, a beverage which Islām has designated as forbidden should not be referred to with a good name so that its evil is established in the hearts of people and they do not incline towards it.

1741.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not say 'al-karm', but say: 'al-'inab' or 'al-ḥabalah'." (Muslim, Dārimī)
1741.commentary: Al-ḥabalah refers to a grape tree or, according to others, the root or branch of a grape tree.

1742.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A woman should not embrace another woman and then describe her to her husband so that he can visualise her." (Bukhārī, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1742.commentary: The word tubāshir means to touch or view. Hence the ḥadīth forbids a woman from touching the body of another woman with her own body or viewing it, and then describing its qualities to her husband. This is a shameful and dishonourable practice because when a man learns of another woman's beauty, he will be inclined to her. This may result in the ruining of marriages or at the least, it will draw impermissible thoughts in the minds of men. While this ḥadīth refers to a woman's beauty, the law will apply equally to a man. Hence the strength and beauty of a man's body should not be described to a strange woman.

1743.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "None of you should say: 'O Allāh, forgive me if You will. O Allāh, be merciful to me if You will.' Rather, he should ask with conviction because none can compel Him." A narration of Muslim has: "Rather, he should ask with conviction and intense yearning because nothing is too great for Allāh to give." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah)
1743.commentary: These aḥādīth mean that a person should supplicate with conviction and certitude. He should not exhibit weakness in his request nor leave the request to Allāh's will because this gives an impression that one is independent of Allāh. The reality is that every person is fully dependent on Allāh and nothing is difficult for Allāh. According to other scholars, these aḥādīth mean that one should be hopeful of acceptance when supplicating.

1744.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When any of you supplicates, he should ask with firm conviction. He should not say, 'O Allāh, give me if You will,' because none can compel Him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1744.commentary: This ḥadīth reinforces the previous one about supplicating with conviction.

1745.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not say, 'What Allāh wills and so-and-so wills.' Rather, say: 'What Allāh wills, and then what so-and-so wills.'" (Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1745.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that it is not permissible to unify the creation of Allāh with Allāh in any action because they cannot be equal; Allāh is far superior.

1746.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) disliked sleeping before 'Ishā' and engaging in conversations after 'Ishā'." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1746.commentary: During the days of ignorance, people would engage in lengthy futile discussions late into the night. Such behaviour not only wastes time but may also cause one to miss the Fajr ṣalāh due to tiredness. The Messenger therefore advised that one should end one's day with the 'Ishā' ṣalāh. This will enable one to awaken for Fajr and Tahajjud more easily. 'Umar used to caution and even reprimand those who engaged in futile discussions after 'Ishā'.

1747.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), towards the end of his life, once offered the 'Ishā' ṣalāh. When he completed it with salām he said: "Do you see this night? No one on the surface of the earth today will be alive a 100 years from now." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Ḥākim)
1747.commentary: This was a prophecy of the Messenger and it transpired as he had foretold. The Messenger explained that all the Ṣaḥābah who lived at that time would pass away before 100 years had passed. The last Ṣaḥābī to leave this world was Abū Ṭufail Āmir ibn Wā'il who passed away in 110 Hijrī. This was exactly 100 years from the time the Messenger made the prophecy. Scholars state that the ḥadīth also urges the believers towards good deeds because life is short and death is always imminent.

1748.text: They waited for the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), but he only emerged close to midnight and then led them in ṣalāh – the 'Ishā' ṣalāh. He then addressed us saying: 'Listen, people have performed their ṣalāh and gone to sleep, but you were considered to be in ṣalāh for as long as you waited for ṣalāh.'" (Bukhārī)
1748.commentary: This ḥadīth highlights that Islāmic knowledge may be imparted to people after the 'Ishā' ṣalāh.

1749.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses, and he then spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until the morning." Another narration has: "until she returns (to her husband)." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1749.commentary: The ḥadīth informs us that it is a severe sin for a woman to ignore the call of her husband for conjugal relations without any valid reason such as sickness, obligatory fasting, menstruation, etc. Such a response from her side provokes the curses of the angels and worse still, the anger of Allāh. It also sparks enmity in the marriage and may cause the husband to satisfy his desires elsewhere. Scholars state that if a woman knows that her husband will not be angered by her refusal to satisfy his desires, the stipulated warning in this ḥadīth will not apply. However, it will still be better for her to accede to his request so that love and harmony may prevail between them.

1750.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "It is not permissible for a woman to fast while her husband is present except with his permission, and she may not permit anyone to enter his house without his permission." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1750.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that a woman may not engage in any Nafl worship without her husband's consent. In broader terms it also indicates that a husband's rights take preference to optional acts of worship because the former are Wājib and the latter are Nafl, and fulfilling marital relations preserves modesty and dignity. The second portion of the ḥadīth informs us that a woman may not permit into her home any man whom her husband does not approve of, whether he is a family member or not. The reason for this is that there may be some enmity between the two men and this will create enmity between the couple.

1751.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Does any of you not fear that Allāh may turn his head into that of a donkey or make his form into that of a donkey if he were to raise his head before the Imām?" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1751.commentary: Ṣalāh is a form of worship which demands obedience and conformity, hence one should not perform it in haste or precede the Imām in any posture. Some scholars say that this warning is not literal but figurative. In other words, one who precedes the Imām will become weak in understanding and intelligence like a donkey. Other scholars such as Khaṭṭābī and Ibn Ḥajar state that a physical transformation of the body is also possible. Ibn Ḥajar mentioned the incident of a certain ḥadīth scholar who always taught from behind a veil. When one of his students insisted to see his face, it turned out to be that of a donkey. The scholar explained that he once tested the truth of this ḥadīth by preceding the Imām from sajdah, and Allāh transformed his face into that of a donkey.

1752.text: Placing the hand on the hip in ṣalāh is prohibited." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1752.commentary: Scholars have mentioned various reasons for this prohibition: 1. On the plains of Qiyāmah, those destined for Hell-fire will place their hands on their hips while waiting for the reckoning to commence. 2. When Shaiṭān was disgraced and expelled from Paradise, he adopted this stance. 3. It is the stance of the proud and arrogant.

1753.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Ṣalāh should not be performed when food is present, or when a person has the urge to relieve himself." (Muslim)
1753.commentary: Performing ṣalāh when one is hard-pressed to eat or relieve oneself is disliked because one's focus will be diverted from Allāh. Similarly, every such action which disturbs a person's concentration during ṣalāh should be completed before commencing ṣalāh. However, if the time for ṣalāh is limited and there is a fear that the ṣalāh may be missed completely, then one should perform the ṣalāh and then perform that action.

1754.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "What is wrong with some people that they raise their gaze to the sky in their ṣalāh?" He issued a stern warning against this to the extent that he said: "They should abstain from this or their eyesight will be snatched away." (Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah, Aḥmad)
1754.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that a person should be focussed when performing ṣalāh and should not look around at others or at the sky above. Ṣalāh is a dialogue between the worshipper and his Creator, hence one should not engage in any such actions or thoughts which contradict this. If one looks around to the extent that one's chest turns away from the Qiblah, his ṣalāh will be nullified.

1755.text: I asked the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) about looking around in ṣalāh. He said: 'It is a means of Shaiṭān snatching away from a person's ṣalāh.'" (Bukhārī, Tirmidhī, Ḥākim)
1755.commentary: Looking around while in ṣalāh is contrary to the devotion and concentration that ṣalāh demands. One who does so unfortunately loses the benefits of ṣalāh because he has allowed Shaiṭān to snatch away the essence of his ṣalāh.

1756.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said to me: 'Beware of turning around in ṣalāh because it is a cause of destruction. If you have to do so, then let it be in Nafl ṣalāh but not in Farḍ ṣalāh.'" (Tirmidhī)
1756.commentary: One who looks around in ṣalāh loses his focus and thereby ruins his rewards in the Hereafter. The ḥadīth does not permit looking around in Nafl ṣalāh, rather it implies that doing so in Nafl ṣalāh is less sinful than in Farḍ ṣalāh.

1757.narrator: Abū Marthad Kannāz ibn al-Ḥuṣayn (رضي الله عنه)
1757.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Do not perform ṣalāh towards graves nor sit on them." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Nasa'ī)
1757.commentary: Performing ṣalāh facing a grave in order to honour the occupant of that grave is kufr (disbelief). Doing so without that intention is Makrūh Taḥrīmī. It is not permissible to do so even in the latter case because onlookers may consider that one is worshipping the grave. We are prohibited from sitting on graves because this is disrespectful and contradicts the honour and dignity which Islām demands for every person.

1758.narrator: Abū al-Juhaym 'Abdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṣimmah al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه)
1758.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If the person who walks across one offering ṣalāh only knew the sin that he is committing, it would have been better for him to remain waiting for forty than to walk across him." The narrator said: "I do not know whether he said forty days, forty months or forty years." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, Aḥmad)
1758.commentary: A person performing ṣalāh is focused towards the Qiblah and in dialogue with Allāh. A person who walks across him distracts him from his purpose and has therefore been warned against doing so. Scholars state that forty in this ḥadīth refers to forty years.

1759.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When the iqāmah for the ṣalāh is given, no ṣalāh besides the obligatory may be performed." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1759.commentary: The wisdom of this ruling is that a person should attempt to complete his Sunnah and Nafl ṣalāhs before the Imām commences, so that he may join the Farḍ ṣalāh with full devotion and acquire the great rewards of the first takbīr. In addition, an obligatory action takes preference over an optional one. According to Imām Abū Ḥanīfah and Imām Mālik, this ḥadīth excludes Fajr ṣalāh, hence according to them it is permissible to perform the Sunnah ṣalāh of Fajr after the Imām has commenced the Farḍ ṣalāh. According to Imām Shāfi'ī and Imām Aḥmad, it is Makrūh to perform any Sunnah or Nafl ṣalāhs once the Imām has commenced the Farḍ ṣalāh.

1760.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not select only the night of Jumu'ah over other nights for performing ṣalāh, and do not select only the day of Jumu'ah over other days for fasting, unless it is part of the fast which you normally keep." (Muslim, Ḥākim)
1760.commentary: Various reasons have been given by the scholars for not fasting exclusively on the day of Jumu'ah: 1. One should focus on the other forms of worship on this day such as a special ghusl, proceeding early to the masjid, listening attentively to the sermon, and engaging in du'ā', durūd, dhikr and Nafl ṣalāh. By not fasting, one will have additional strength to exert oneself in these forms of worship. 2. Jumu'ah has been called the day of 'Īd and one cannot fast on the day of 'Īd. 3. The Muslims should not exaggerate the greatness of Jumu'ah as the Jews and Christians exaggerated their days of merit.

1761.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "None of you should fast on the day of Jumu'ah unless he also fasts a day before or after." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)

1762.text: Muḥammad ibn 'Abbād narrates: "I asked Jābir (رضي الله عنه): 'Did the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) forbid fasting on the day of Jumu'ah?' He replied: 'Yes.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)

1763.narrator: Umm al-Mu'minīn Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith (رضي الله عنها)
1763.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) visited her on the day of Jumu'ah and she was fasting. He asked: "Did you fast yesterday?" She replied: "No." He asked: "Do you intend fasting tomorrow?" She replied: "No." He said: "Then break your fast." (Bukhārī, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)

1764.text: Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) and 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) narrate that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited continuous fasting. (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1764.commentary: Fasting for two or more days without eating or drinking between them is prohibited because it induces weakness in the body and this is harmful for other acts of worship. Such fasting causes difficulty to a Muslim, whereas Allāh desires ease.

1765.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited continuous fasting. The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) said to him: "But you fast continuously." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) replied: "I am not like you. I am provided with food and drink." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1765.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) was permitted to fast for days at a time without eating or drinking because of the following reasons: 1. The Messenger (ﷺ) was granted food and drink by Allāh from Paradise. 2. The Messenger (ﷺ) was given patience, willpower and physical strength by Allāh. 3. According to Ibn Qayyim, the Messenger (ﷺ) was showered with such divine radiance from Allāh while fasting that made him independent of food and drink.

1766.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "For one of you to sit on a burning coal which burns his clothes and reaches his skin is better than sitting on a grave." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1766.commentary: It is not permissible to sit on a grave as this is contrary to the respect Islām demands for fellow human beings.

1767.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited plastering over a grave, sitting on it, and building on it." (Muslim)
1767.commentary: It is not permissible to plaster a grave from the inside or outside, or to build a dome or structure above it because it entails unnecessary wastage of wealth. In fact, if something has been built on a grave, it is compulsory to remove it as 'Alī (رضي الله عنه) once did upon the command of the Messenger (ﷺ).

1768.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a slave escapes from his master, he loses his Islāmic protection." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1768.commentary: A slave who escapes from Dār al-Islām to Dār al-Ḥarb and becomes a renegade, loses all the rights and protection he enjoyed under Islām and should be killed.

1769.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a slave escapes from his master, no ṣalāh of his is accepted." Another narration has: "He has committed kufr (disbelief)." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1769.commentary: "No ṣalāh of his is accepted" means that he will not be rewarded by Allāh for performing ṣalāh. "He has committed kufr (disbelief)" means that he has been unappreciative of the bounties of his master, or has committed an action that is tantamount to disbelief. One who is entrusted with a particular job or responsibility should fulfil its requirements to the best of his ability.

1770.text: The Quraysh were very concerned about the Makzūmī woman who had committed theft and said: 'Who will speak to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) about her?' They said: 'Who will have the courage to do so except Usāmah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ)?' So Usāmah spoke to him and the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Are you interceding in one of the penal laws of Allāh?' He then stood up and addressed the people saying: 'The nations before you were destroyed because when a noble person among them committed theft, they left him alone, but when a weak person committed theft, they meted out the punishment to him. By Allāh, if Fāṭimah the daughter of Muḥammad were to commit theft, I will cut off her hand.'" Another narration has: "The face of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) changed colour and he said: 'Are you interceding in one of the penal laws of Allāh?' Usāmah (رضي الله عنه) said: 'Seek forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allāh.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) gave the order regarding the woman and her hand was cut off." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1770.commentary: The woman referred to here was the daughter of the brother of Abū Salamah (رضي الله عنه). The ḥadīth teaches us that Islām is a religion of justice and equality. It does not differentiate between the rich and poor regarding the implementation of laws. One may intercede in a case which demands the implementation of penal law before it reaches an Islāmic court. After it reaches the court, intercession will not be valid. The ḥadīth also highlights the virtue of Usāmah ibn Zayd (رضي الله عنه) and his status in the sight of the Messenger (ﷺ).

1771.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Beware of two actions which provoke curses." The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) asked: "What are the two actions which provoke curses?" He replied: "One who relieves himself where people walk or seek shade." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1771.commentary: This ḥadīth teaches us that a Muslim should not harm or inconvenience others by relieving himself in communal places.

1772.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited urinating in stagnant water." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1772.commentary: Stagnant water here refers to a small quantity of water such as a pond. It is prohibited to urinate or defecate in such water because it will render the water impure. One should also not urinate close to such water because the impurity may reach the water and contaminate it. Scholars state that one should not even urinate in flowing water because if many people do so it will also become impure after a time.

1773.text: His father brought him to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and said: "I gave this son of mine a slave that I owned." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) asked: "Did you give all your children a similar gift?" He replied: "No." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Then take the slave back." Another narration has: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) asked: 'Did you do this to all your children?' He replied: 'No.' He said: 'Fear Allāh and treat your children equally.' My father returned and took back the charity." Another narration has: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) asked: 'O Bashīr, do you have other children?' He replied: 'Yes.' He asked: 'Did you give a similar gift to all of them?' He replied: 'No.' He said: 'Then do not make me a witness to this because I cannot be a witness to an injustice.'" Another narration has: "Do not make me a witness to an injustice." Another narration has: "Make someone else a witness to this." He then said: "Would you not like all of them to be equal in their obedience to you?" He replied: "Yes, indeed." He said: "Then do not do that." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1773.commentary: Favouring some children over others causes enmity and disunity between them, hence it should be avoided at all costs. According to Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله), such a gift in which some are favoured over others is Ḥarām and not valid. According to the other Imāms, the gift will be valid but it will be Makrūh. However, if a parent assists a particular child due to some need, such as poverty, then there is no harm.

1774.narrator: Zaynab bint Abī Salamah (رضي الله عنها)
1774.text: I went to visit Umm Ḥabībah (رضي الله عنها), the wife of the Messenger (ﷺ), when her father, Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb (رضي الله عنه) passed away. She asked for some yellow-coloured perfume or something like that and applied some of it to a slave-girl. She then rubbed some of it on her own cheeks and said: 'By Allāh, I have no need for perfume, however, I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying while on the pulpit: 'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allāh and the Last Day to mourn over a deceased for more than three days besides her husband, for whom she may do so for four months and ten days.' Zaynab said: 'I then went to visit Zaynab bint Jaḥsh (رضي الله عنها) when her brother passed away. She asked for some perfume and applied some of it. She then said: 'Listen, by Allāh, I have no need for perfume, however, I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying while on the pulpit: 'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allāh and the Last Day to mourn over a deceased for more than three days besides her husband, for whom she may do so for four months and ten days.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1774.commentary: In these incidents the blessed wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) applied perfume in order to display the impermissibility for a woman to mourn for more than three days for anyone besides her husband. A woman should mourn for this extended period for her husband because of his noble right over her as a husband, the bond of love that existed between them and to establish that she is not pregnant with his child.

1775.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited an urban-dweller to sell on behalf of a rural-dweller even if he is a blood brother." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1775.commentary: The ḥadīth commands that an urban-dweller should not sell an item on behalf of a rural-dweller by agreement between them by raising the price when its market-value rises because this creates a monopoly and causes harm to the general public. However, if the item is not one of necessity in the area or not in great demand, then it will be permissible for the urban-dweller to sell it.

1776.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not go out to meet goods before they reach the markets." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1776.commentary: This ḥadīth commands that trade caravans should not be intercepted before reaching the market for purchase at a lower price because this prevents the sellers from ascertaining the true market value of the goods. Such conduct also does harm to the genuine buyers and sellers and allows people to generate excessive profits.

1777.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not go ahead to meet caravans, and an urban-dweller should not sell on behalf of a rural-dweller." Ṭā'ūs asked: "What does it mean that 'an urban-dweller should not sell on behalf of a rural-dweller'?" He replied: "He should not be his agent." (Bukhārī, Muslim)

1778.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited an urban-dweller to sell on behalf of a rural-dweller, offering to purchase in order to raise the price, purchase in the midst of another brother's purchase, sending a marriage proposal when another brother has proposed, and for a woman to ask for her sister to be divorced so that she may take her place." Another narration has: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited from going ahead to meet the trade caravans, an urban-dweller selling on behalf of a rural-dweller, a woman demanding that her sister be divorced, raising the price after the transaction has already been concluded, and he prohibited offering to purchase in order to raise the price, and leaving milk in the udders of an animal." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasa'ī)
1778.commentary: Tanājush means to raise the price of an item while having no intention to purchase it. This happens when a seller hires a person disguised as a buyer who pretends to purchase the item at a higher price, while having no intention to purchase it. It is forbidden because it deceives potential buyers into believing that the item is in demand at a higher price. It is not permissible for a seller to offer an item to a buyer at a lower price when the latter has already agreed to purchase it from another buyer at a higher price. It is forbidden to send a marriage proposal to a woman when another man has proposed for her and not yet received an answer because this generates enmity between people. A woman should not plan or request the divorce of another woman so that the former may then marry the latter's husband. One should not leave milk in the udders of an animal with the intention that a potential buyer will be deceived into believing that it gives a large quantity of milk. Transactions which create difficulty for the general public or which generate enmity between traders and merchants should be avoided.

1779.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "You should not purchase in the midst of another purchase, and you should not send a marriage proposal when another brother has proposed unless he gives permission." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)

1780.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A believer is a brother of another believer and it is therefore not lawful for a believer to purchase in the midst of another brother's purchase, and he should not send a marriage proposal when another brother has proposed unless he withdraws." (Muslim)

1781.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) likes three things for you and dislikes three things for you. He likes that you worship Him, that you do not ascribe any partners with Him, and that you hold to the rope of Allāh together without disuniting between yourselves. He dislikes idle chatter, excessive questions, and squandering of wealth." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Mālik)
1781.commentary: Excessive questions for the purposes of disputing and sparking enmity are not permissible. The Qur'ān also forbade this type of behaviour by highlighting the excessive questions posed by the Banī Isrā'īl. Allāh (ﷻ) has created wealth for the functioning and operation of this worldly life. It should be utilised in the correct way by giving zakāt, lillāh and purchasing items of necessity such as food, clothing, etc. Squandering of wealth by using it in impermissible avenues, purchasing items which are useless or futile, spending exorbitant amounts on personal beautification and so forth is prohibited.

1782.text: Warrād, the scribe of al-Mughīrān ibn Shu'bah (رضي الله عنه), narrates: "Al-Mughīrah dictated to me in a letter which he wrote to Mu'āwiyah (رضي الله عنه) that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to say after every obligatory ṣalāh: 'There is none worthy of worship besides Allāh. He is one and has no partner. His is the sovereignty and to Him belongs all praise. He has power over everything. O Allāh, none can withhold what You give and none can give what You withhold. The influence of any person who has it is of no avail against You.' He also wrote to him saying: 'He prohibited idle chatter, squandering of wealth and excessive questions. He prohibited disobedience to mothers, burying of daughters alive, refusing to give what is due upon you and demanding what is not rightfully yours.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1782.commentary: This du'ā' was mentioned and explained previously. See ḥadīth 1416. Aḥādīth were written and recorded from the era of the Ṣaḥābah.

1783.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "None of you should point a weapon at his brother because it is possible that Shaiṭān may snatch it from his hand and thereby cause him to fall into a pit of the Hell-fire." A narration of Muslim has: Abū al-Qāsim (ﷺ) said: "If someone points a piece of iron at his brother, the angels curse him until he puts it down even if it is his blood brother." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Ḥākim)
1783.commentary: The ḥadīth warns against pointing a weapon towards another believer because Shaiṭān may cause it to slip from his hand resulting in injury or death. This is not impossible since Shaiṭān is forever waiting to cause harm and difficulty to a Muslim.

1784.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited the handing over of an unsheathed sword." (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1784.commentary: The ḥadīth warns us against handing over an unsheathed sword because it may easily slip causing injury. In addition, it is Ḥarām to create fear in the heart of a believer. Scholars explain that a sword, knife or any sharp object should be handed over by placing the handle towards the person it is being given to so that no harm may result.

1785.text: Abū al-Sha'thā' narrates: "We were sitting with Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) in the masjid and the mu'adhdhin called out the adhān. A man stood up and walked out of the masjid. Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) watched him until he left the masjid. Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) then said: 'This person has disobeyed Abū al-Qāsim (ﷺ).'" (Muslim)
1785.commentary: One should not unnecessarily leave the masjid after the adhān has been called because it is possible that one may be deprived of performing the ṣalāh altogether, and it may also create evil thoughts in the minds of others. However, if one has a valid excuse, then it will be permissible.

1786.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who is offered perfume should not refuse it because it is light to carry and fragrant in scent." (Muslim)
1786.commentary: One should not refuse the gift of 'itr because it is a pleasant gift. Ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) narrated that a person should not refuse three things: a pillow, 'itr and milk. Giving 'itr as a gift and applying it especially before attending a gathering is Mustaḥab.

1787.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) would not refuse perfume." (Bukhārī, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1787.commentary: 'Allāmah 'Ainī (رحمه الله) stated that the Messenger (ﷺ) loved perfume because he would interact with the angels who dislike offensive odours. Scholars state that the ḥadīth teaches the basic principle that one should not reject the gift of 'itr or any other such beneficial item which is easy to give and receive.

1788.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) heard a person praising someone excessively. He (ﷺ) said: 'You have destroyed him - or you have broken the man's back.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1788.commentary: The ḥadīth means that praising a person to his face may result in him developing pride, a quality which will destroy his spirituality and rewards in the Hereafter. Praise is of three types: 1. Praising an individual to his face is impermissible. 2. Praising an individual in his absence hoping that such praise will reach him is also impermissible. 3. Praising an individual without any intention of such praise reaching him is permissible. The ḥadīth advises us that if it is necessary to praise an individual, then one should say that he thinks him to be praiseworthy. That is, he should not praise him with certainty and conviction because Allāh (ﷻ) is the only one who knows the internal status and goodness of a person.

1789.text: A person was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and another praised him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Destruction to you! You have severed your friend's neck,' and repeated it several times. 'If you really need to praise someone, say: 'I think he is like this or like that', if you think him to be like that. Only Allāh can call him to account and none can claim purity before Allāh.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)

1790.text: Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith narrates from al-Miqdād (رضي الله عنه) that a man began praising 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه), so al-Miqdād (رضي الله عنه) went forward, sat up on his knees and began to throw pebbles on his face. 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه) asked him: "What are you doing?" He replied: "The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'When you see people praising others, then throw dust in their faces.'" (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1790.commentary: These aḥādīth prohibit it, but there are many other authentic aḥādīth which permit it. Scholars state that the method of reconciling between these various aḥādīth is to say that if the person who is praised has perfect īmān and conviction, self discipline and complete knowledge by virtue of which he is neither tempted nor deceived by such praise, and his soul does not play around with him, then it is neither unlawful nor undesirable. But if it is feared that he will be overcome by any of these matters, it is strongly undesirable to praise him to his face.

1791.text: 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه) set out for Syria. When he reached Sargh, the army commanders, Abū 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (رضي الله عنه) and his companions met him and informed him that a plague had broken out in Syria. Ibn 'Abbās (رضي الله عنه) said: "'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said to me: 'Call the first of the Muhājirīn.' I called them and 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) consulted them. He informed them of the plague that had broken out in Syria. They differed in opinion. Some of them said: 'You set out for a particular purpose and we do not think that you should divert from it.' Others said: 'With you are people and the Ṣaḥābah of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). We do not think you should expose them to this plague.' He said: 'You may go.' He then said: 'Call the Anṣār.' I called them and he consulted with them. They differed among themselves as the Muhājirīn had done. He said: 'You may go.' He then said: 'Call the elders of the Quraysh who migrated before the conquest of Makkah.' I called them and they all unanimously said: 'We think that you should return with the people and not expose them to this plague.' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) then announced to the people: 'I will be returning tomorrow morning, so you people should also prepare to return in the morning.' Abū 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ (رضي الله عنه) said to him: 'Are you fleeing from the decree of Allāh?' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said: 'If only someone besides you had made such a statement.' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) disliked opposing him. 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said: 'Yes. We are fleeing from the decree of Allāh and going towards the decree of Allāh. If you had camels and they descended into a valley which had two sections, one of which was fertile while the other was barren; if you were to graze them in the fertile area, will you not be grazing them by the decree of Allāh, and if you were to graze them in the barren area, will you not be grazing them by the decree of Allāh?' 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Auf (رضي الله عنه) who had been busy elsewhere then arrived and said: 'I have some knowledge regarding this. I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: 'When you hear of a plague in an area, do not go to it, and if you are in an area where a plague erupts, do not flee from it.' 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) then praised Allāh (ﷻ) and returned (to Madīnah)." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1791.commentary: A leader should consult his subjects but is not obligated to accept their opinions. One should avoid harmful places and situations. A leader should lead and guide his subjects to that which is in their best interests and he should protect them from that which may harm them.

1792.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When you hear of a plague in a particular area, do not enter it, and if it erupts in an area where you are, do not leave it." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1792.commentary: A believer should take every means of protection from illness and disease. For this reason, he should not enter an area of a plague because he may be afflicted with it. Similarly, he should not leave an area of a plague because it may spread from him to others.

1793.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Refrain from the seven destructive sins." The Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) asked: "What are they, O Messenger of Allāh?" He replied: "Ascribing partners with Allāh, black magic, killing a person whom Allāh has forbidden unless for justice, consuming usury (interest), consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing from the battlefield, and slandering chaste, innocent believing women." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd)
1793.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned previously. See ḥadīth 1615. It is repeated here to highlight the prohibition and severity of black magic. That it is mentioned immediately after ascribing partners with Allāh (ﷻ) and before killing another unjustly, proves the severity of its sin.

1794.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited travelling with the Qur'ān to enemy lands." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1794.commentary: It is prohibited to travel with a Qur'ān to enemy lands when one fears that the enemy may disrespect it or mock at it. If there is no such fear, this prohibition does not apply.

1795.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who drinks from a silver utensil is gulping down the Hell-fire into his stomach." Another narration of Muslim has: "One who eats or drinks from a gold and silver utensil." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1795.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned previously. See ḥadīth 778. It teaches us that it is not permissible to utilise gold and silver utensils for eating, drinking, performing wuḍū' or applying 'itr. It is forbidden for men to wear gold watches and rings or to write with golden pens.

1796.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited us from silk, silk brocade, and drinking from gold and silver utensils." He said: "They are for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter." Another narration has: Ḥudhayfah (رضي الله عنه) said: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Do not wear silk or silk brocade. Do not drink from gold and silver utensils. And do not eat from such plates." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1796.commentary: Another narration states that one who wears silk in this world will be deprived of wearing it in the Hereafter. Silk garments are only forbidden for men and not women.

1797.text: Anas ibn Sīrīn narrates: "I was with Anas ibn Mālik (رضي الله عنه) and a group of Magians when some fālūdhaj was brought in a silver utensil, but Anas (رضي الله عنه) did not eat from it. The person was told to change the utensil so he placed it in a wooden utensil and brought it. Anas (رضي الله عنه) then ate from it." (Bayhaqī)
1797.commentary: If food has been placed in a gold or silver utensil, it should only be eaten after being transferred to another utensil. The aḥādīth of this chapter reveal that Islām encourages simplicity in food, drinks, household appliances, etc. Extravagance, wastage and imitation of the ways of the disbelievers is prohibited.

1798.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) prohibited men from using saffron." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasa'ī)

1799.narrator: Abdullāh ibn 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه)
1799.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saw me wearing two yellow-coloured garments. He said: 'Did your mother order you to wear this?' I replied: 'Should I wash them?' He said: 'No, rather burn them.'" Another narration has: "These are the garments of the disbelievers, so do not wear them." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1799.commentary: The Messenger's (ﷺ) instruction to burn them was to inform the Ṣaḥābī of the severity of the sin and to prohibit others from doing so. The reason for prohibiting such clothing for men is that this colour is commonly used by women to beautify themselves, hence men should not imitate them. While these aḥādīth prohibit the wearing of saffron-coloured garments for men, other aḥādīth permit it. Scholars have explained this contradiction as follows: 1. It was initially permissible to wear such garments, but this law was later abrogated for men. 2. Those narrations that permit it refer to clothing that was coloured with saffron for fragrance purposes and after washing, very little of the colour remains.

1800.text: I memorised from the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ): 'None can be an orphan after puberty, and none should remain silent from morning to night.'" (Abū Dāwūd) In explaining this ḥadīth, al-Khaṭṭābī (رحمه الله) said: "Remaining silent was one of the customs of jāhilīyyah, hence they were prohibited from this in Islām and ordered to engage in the remembrance of Allāh and beneficial discussions."
1800.commentary: These aḥādīth teach us that silence is not a form of worship in Islām. Yes, abstaining from futile talk, backbiting, slander, gossip, lies, etc is necessary and will draw divine rewards, however silence in itself is not to be assumed as a form of worship. The ḥadīth also explains that the laws pertaining to orphans will only apply to a child who has not reached the age of puberty.

1801.text: Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim narrates: "Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (رضي الله عنه) once went to a woman from the Aḥmas tribe called Zaynab and noticed that she was not speaking. He asked: 'Why is she not speaking?' They replied: 'She made the intention not to speak.' He said to her: 'Speak, because this (silence) is not lawful. This is from the customs of jāhilīyyah.' So she began speaking." (Bukhārī)

1802.narrator: Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (رضي الله عنه)
1802.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who ascribes lineage to someone other than his own father while knowing that that person is not his father, then Paradise is unlawful for him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)

1803.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not disown your fathers. One who disowns his father commits disbelief." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1803.commentary: One who attributes his lineage to someone other than his father and assumes this as permissible commits an act of kufr (disbelief). Sometimes a high ranking person is ashamed to link himself to his father because the latter may be a poor and humble individual, but this is an unjust denial of the person through whom one came into existence. Islām regards the knowledge of lineages and relatives as important because it enables one to fulfil the necessary rights due upon people. It also helps to protect the laws of marriage because if one cannot identify close relatives, one may easily marry a person whom Islām has forbidden to marry.

1804.text: Yazīd ibn Sharīk ibn Ṭāriq narrates: "I saw 'Alī (رضي الله عنه) delivering a sermon from the pulpit and I heard him saying: 'By Allāh, we have no book to read besides the Book of Allāh and what is in this scroll. He unfolded it and it contained information on the ages of camels (for zakāt) and compensation for those who suffer injuries. In it the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'Madīnah is a sanctuary from 'Ayr to Thaur. Therefore, one who initiates an innovation (bid'ah) in it or gives refuge to an innovator will earn the curse of Allāh, the angels and people. On the day of Qiyāmah, Allāh will not accept repentance or ransom from him. The pledge of protection given by a Muslim, even the lowest of them, is valid. One who breaks the pledge of a Muslim earns the curse of Allāh, the angels and all people. On the day of Qiyāmah, Allāh will not accept repentance or ransom from him. One who claims lineage from other than his father, or a slave who claims another as his master, earns the curse of Allāh, the angels and all people. On the day of Qiyāmah, Allāh will not accept repentance or ransom from him.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1804.commentary: The region between the two mountains mentioned in this ḥadīth is sacred, hence according to Imām Shāfi'ī (رحمه الله), Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله) and Imām Mālik (رحمه الله) no animal can be hunted here and no tree may be cut down. According to Imām Abū Ḥanīfah (رحمه الله), no such action should be done which contradicts the sanctity of the area, however one may hunt or cut down a tree. The statement of 'Alī (رضي الله عنه) that he possessed nothing besides the Qur'ān and the scroll is a clear proof against the Shī'a who claim that the Messenger (ﷺ) had imparted to him some secret knowledge of Islām.

1805.text: He heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "One who knowingly claims lineage to other than his father, commits an act of disbelief. One who lays claim to what is not his is not of us. He should prepare his abode in the Hell-fire. One who accuses another of disbelief or says: 'O enemy of Allāh!', when it is not the case, it will revert to him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1805.commentary: "He should prepare his abode in the Hell-fire," can either be interpreted as a curse or a notification of punishment in the Hereafter.

1806.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) has a sense of discontent and His discontent manifests when a person commits an act which Allāh has made unlawful for him." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1806.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned previously. See ḥadīth 64.

1807.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who takes an oath by saying: 'By al-Lāt and al-'Uzzā', should say, 'There is none worthy of worship besides Allāh.' One who says to his friend: 'Come, let us gamble', should give ṣadaqah." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1807.commentary: One who mistakenly takes an oath on false deities should recite the kalimah in expiation, and if one did so knowingly believing it to be true, then he should recite the kalimah to renew his īmān because he has committed an act of disbelief. One who invites another to commit such a sin as gambling should make amends by giving some of his wealth in ṣadaqah.

1808.text: One morning, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) spoke about Dajjāl lowering and raising his voice until we thought that he was in a nearby date-palm grove. When we went to see him later on, he realised our anxiety and asked: 'What has happened with you?' We replied: 'O Messenger of Allāh, you spoke about Dajjāl in the morning lowering and raising your voice until we thought that he was in a nearby date-palm grove.' He said: 'Other things cause me to fear more for you than Dajjāl. If he appears while I am present among you, I will defeat him for your benefit. If he appears while I am not present among you, each person will have to defend himself and Allāh will be my deputy for every Muslim. He is a youth with curly hair and his one eye will be protruding. I can compare him to 'Abd al-'Uzzā ibn Qaṭan. Anyone of you who meets him should recite the beginning verses of Sūrah al-Kahf. He will appear on the road between Syria and Iraq and spread corruption to the right and left. O servants of Allāh, remain steadfast!' We asked: 'O Messenger of Allāh, how long will he remain on earth?' He replied: 'Forty days. One day will be equal to a year; one day will be equal to a month; one day will be like a Jumu'ah, and the rest of his days will be the same as yours.' We asked: 'O Messenger of Allāh, the day which will be equal to a year, will it suffice us to perform ṣalāh for one day?' He replied: 'No, you will have to calculate.' We asked: 'O Messenger of Allāh, how fast will he travel on earth?' He replied: 'Like rain propelled by wind. He will go to a people and invite them. They will believe him and respond to his call. He will order the heavens and it will rain, and order the earth and it will produce vegetation. Their grazing animals will return to them in the evening with the highest humps, fullest udders and broadest flanks. He will then go to a people and invite them but they will reject his message. He will depart from them and they will be struck by a drought and will be left with no wealth whatsoever. He will pass by a completely deserted land and order it saying: 'Reveal your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like a swarm of bees. He will then call a youth in his prime, strike him swiftly with a sword and cut him into two pieces. He will then call the youth who will walk towards him with his face beaming and laughing.' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) continued: 'While these events are unfolding, Allāh will send al-Masīḥ ibn Maryam (عليه السلام). He will descend on the white minaret to the east of Damascus, wearing two coloured garments and with his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops of water will fall, and when he raises his head, drops like pearls will flow from it. Every disbeliever who gets a whiff of his breath will die, and his breath will reach as far as his eyes can see. He will then search for Dajjāl until he finds him at the door of Ludd, and kill him. 'Īsā (عليه السلام) will then go to a people whom Allāh had protected from Dajjāl. He will pass his hand on their faces and inform them of their ranks in Paradise...'" (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1808.commentary: This ḥadīth explains the evil of Dajjāl and the various tribulations that people will face when he emerges. 'Allāmah Ṭībī (رحمه الله) stated that those who recite Sūrah Kahf will be protected from the evil of Dajjāl just as the youth mentioned in this Sūrah were protected from the tyrant king of their time. The ḥadīth mentions that 'Īsā (عليه السلام) will descend towards the east of Syria. Some scholars interpret this as the area of Bait al-Maqdis. During his reign, justice will prevail and there will be abundant blessings. After him, conditions will deteriorate drastically, until such a time when no believer will remain on the face of the earth. This will herald the coming of Qiyāmah.

1809.text: Rib'ī ibn Ḥirāsh narrates: "I accompanied Abū Mas'ūd al-Anṣārī to visit Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān (رضي الله عنهم) and Abū Mas'ūd said to him: 'Relate to me what you heard from the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) about Dajjāl.' He replied: 'Dajjāl will appear with water and fire. What the people will assume to be water will actually be fire that burns, and what they assume to be fire will actually be cool, sweet water. Any of you who meet him should jump into what appears as fire because it is actually pure, sweet water.' Abū Mas'ūd said: 'I also heard this.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)

1810.narrator: Abdullāh ibn 'Amr ibn al-'Āṣ (رضي الله عنه)
1810.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Dajjāl will emerge among my Ummah and remain for forty – I do not know whether it will be forty days, forty months or forty years. Allāh will then send 'Īsā ibn Maryam (عليه السلام) who will search for him and destroy him. The people will then remain for seven years without any enmity between them. Allāh will then send a cool breeze from the direction of Syria and it will seize every person who has even an iota of good or īmān in his heart. If any of you were to hide in the depths of a mountain, it will reach you and seize you. The evil people will remain and they will be like swift birds and animals of prey in shedding blood. They will neither recognise good nor dislike evil. Shaiṭān will come to them in human form and say: 'Are you not going to listen?' They will ask: 'What do you command?' He will order them to worship idols. Despite this, they will receive abundant sustenance and will live a comfortable life. The Trumpet will then be blown and every person who hears it will lower one side of his neck and raise the other (to listen). The first to hear it will be a person repairing his camels' water trough. He will fall unconscious and so will everyone around him. Allāh will then send – or he said: 'Allāh will make fall' – rain that will be like dew or a shadow, and the bodies of people will grow (like plants) due to it. The trumpet will be blown again and the people will all be standing and looking around them. It will be said: 'O people, come to your Sustainer. Make them stand, as they are to be questioned.' It will be said: 'Remove those who are destined for Hell-fire.' The angels will ask: 'How many?' It will be said: 'Nine hundred and ninety nine from every thousand.' That will be a day which will turn children grey. That will be a day when the shins will be exposed." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1810.commentary: This ḥadīth explains some of the events prior to Qiyāmah. It is supported by another ḥadīth which mentions that Qiyāmah will not occur until people take the name of Allāh (ﷻ) remain on the earth.

1811.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Dajjāl will set foot upon every single land except for Makkah and Madīnah. Every entrance leading to Makkah and Madīnah is guarded by angels standing in rows. Dajjāl will halt at a swamp near Madīnah and the city will be shaken three times. Allāh will expel every disbeliever and hypocrite from it." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1811.commentary: The effect of these earthquakes will be that those within Madīnah Munawwarah who follow Dajjāl will emerge and join him.

1812.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand Jews of Iṣfahān (in Iran) who will be wearing green robes will follow Dajjāl." (Muslim)

1813.text: She heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "People will flee from Dajjāl into the mountains." (Muslim, Aḥmad)

1814.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "There is no greater tribulation from the time of the creation of Ādam (عليه السلام) to the Final Hour than Dajjāl." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1814.commentary: This is because of his immense evil, deception and the tribulations he will create. Only a few will be safe from his plots.

1815.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When Dajjāl appears, a believer will go towards him. The armed guards of Dajjāl will ask: 'Where are you going?' He will reply: 'I am going towards this one who has emerged.' They will ask: 'Do you not believe in our lord (Dajjāl)?' He will reply: 'Our Lord (Allāh) is not concealed.' They will say: 'Kill him.' They will then say to one another: 'Did your lord not prohibit you from killing someone without his permission?' They will then take him to Dajjāl. When the believer sees him, he will say: 'O people, this is the Dajjāl whom the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) spoke about.' Dajjāl will order that he be laid on his stomach. He will then say: 'Seize him and strike him on his head and face.' The beating will expand his back and stomach. He will ask: 'Do you not believe in me?' He will reply: 'You are the false Messiah.' Dajjāl will then order him to be sawn with a saw from the centre of his head until it separates between his legs. Dajjāl will then walk between the two halves of his body and say to him: 'Stand up,' and he will stand up straight. He will then ask him: 'Do you believe in me?' He will reply: 'Now I am even more convinced (that you are the Dajjāl).' He (the believer) will say: 'O people, he will not be able to do this to anyone else after me.' Dajjāl will seize him in order to slaughter him, but Allāh will place copper between his neck and collarbone and he will be unable to do so. He will grab him by his hands and legs and throw him. People will assume that he has thrown him into the fire, but he will have thrown him into Paradise." The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) then said: "This person will be the greatest martyr in the sight of Allāh." (Muslim)
1815.commentary: This believer will be the greatest martyr because of his immense sacrifice and his proclamation of the truth to the liar, disbeliever and oppressor, Dajjāl. Scholars explain that when he is thrown into the fire, it will become cool for him just as it became cool for Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام).

1816.text: No one asked the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) about Dajjāl more than I did. He said to me: 'He will not harm you.' I said: 'People claim that he will have a mountain of bread and a river of water.' He said: 'He is not worthy of that in the sight of Allāh.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1816.commentary: "He is not worthy of that in the sight of Allāh," means that Dajjāl will not have the strength and ability to mislead the believers through these signs given to him by Allāh. In fact, these very signs will be a testimony of his falsehood. The more he will try to mislead the believers by his deception, the stronger their īmān will become.

1817.text: Anas reported that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said, "Every Messenger warned his community about the one-eyed liar. He is one-eyed and your Sustainer is not one-eyed. Written between his eyes are the letters kāf, fā, rā." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1817.commentary: Every Messenger of Allāh (عليه السلام) warned his people about Dajjāl because of the overwhelming danger he will pose. The Messenger (ﷺ) described him to us in clear terms and stated that every true believer will recognise him by the letters on his forehead. Further, he will be exposed to be a liar and imposter because he will claim to be Lord despite having physical defects. True believers will not fall for his claims because they know that their Sustainer, Allāh (ﷻ), is free of any defects and deficiencies.

1818.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Should I not tell you something about Dajjāl which no Messenger told his people? He is one-eyed. He will bring with him the likeness of Paradise and the Hell-fire. What he refers to as Paradise is actually the Hell-fire." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1818.commentary: Dajjāl will throw those who disbelieve in him into a fire but it will be cool and comfortable for them. In contrast, he will throw his followers into his garden but it will be a means of punishment and suffering for them.

1819.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) spoke about Dajjāl to the people and said: "Allāh is not one-eyed, but al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl is blind in the right eye which is like a protruding grape." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1819.commentary: Various narrations describe the eyes of Dajjāl. In summary, scholars explain that both his eyes will have a defect which will make his deception clear and apparent because the true Sustainer of the worlds, Allāh (ﷻ), is free of defects.

1820.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The Final Hour will not come until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Jews will hide behind rocks and trees. The rocks and trees will say: 'O Muslim! Here is a Jew behind me. Come and kill him!' This excludes the Gharqad tree because it is the tree of the Jews." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1820.commentary: This ḥadīth describes a prophecy close to Qiyāmah when the Muslims will fight the Jews. All the trees and rocks will assist the Muslims except the Gharqad tree which is a thorny tree found in abundance in Palestine. Scholars state that the current settling of Jews in Palestine is part of the culmination of this prophecy because it would have been impossible for the Muslims to fight the Jews when they were dispersed throughout the world. In this final and decisive battle, the Muslims will defeat the Jews by the assistance of Allāh (ﷻ).

1821.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "By that Being in whose control is my life, this world will not come to an end until a man passes by a grave and rolls on it, saying: 'If only I was in the place of this person buried here.' It will not be due to religion but because of the tribulations of the world." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1821.commentary: Close to Qiyāmah, evil, tribulations and calamities will increase to such an extent that people will prefer death to life.

1822.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: The Final Hour will not come until the Euphrates river dries up and exposes a mountain of gold that lies within it. People will fight over it and ninety nine out of every hundred will be killed. Each one of them will say, 'I hope that I will be the one who is saved.' Another narration has: "A time will soon come when the Euphrates river will dry up and expose its treasures of gold. Whoever is present at that time should not take any of it." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1822.commentary: Muslims are advised not to yearn for any of that gold because it will only be a source of killing, suffering and regret.

1823.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "People will leave Madīnah despite the good it contains and only wild beasts and birds will live in it. The last people to be brought for the Final Hour will be two shepherds from the Muzaynah tribe who will be heading towards Madīnah. They will herd their sheep towards it and find it deserted. When they reach Thanīyyat al-Wadā', they will fall on their faces." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1823.commentary: This ḥadīth has been interpreted in two ways. Scholars such as Qāḍī 'Iyāḍ (رحمه الله) and Imām Qurṭubī (رحمه الله) stated that the prophecy in it was fulfilled when the khilāfah was transferred from Madīnah Munawwarah to Iraq and Syria because Madīnah was prosperous and spiritually brimming with scholars at that time. Other scholars say that the prophecy is yet to be fulfilled close to Qiyāmah.

1824.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "At the end of time, one of your khalīfs will distribute wealth without counting it." (Muslim)
1824.commentary: According to some scholars, this khalīf is Imām Mahdī (رحمه الله) who will appear close to Qiyāmah. Other scholars state that it referred to the third khalīf, 'Uthmān (رضي الله عنه). The ḥadīth indicates that during that era there will be great prosperity and the Muslims will dominate in the world. The khalīf will not hoard wealth but spend it freely on his people. It will be a time when justice and good morals will prevail.

1825.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A time will come when a man will go around with gold to give as ṣadaqah but he will find no one to take it from him. One man will be seen followed by forty women who will desire him because of the scarcity of men and an excess of women." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1825.commentary: This ḥadīth mentions two prophecies. Firstly, due to the abundance of wealth, nobody will be prepared to accept ṣadaqah. Secondly, there will be many more women than men on account of wars or increased female births.

1826.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A man purchased a piece of land from another man. The one who purchased it found a jar containing gold on the land. He said to the seller of the land: 'Take your gold. I only purchased the land from you and not the gold.' The one who had owned the land said: 'I sold you the land and whatever it contained.' So they approached a person to resolve their dispute and he said to them: 'Do both of you have children?' One of them said, 'I have a son,' and the other said, 'I have a daughter.' He said: 'Marry the boy to the girl, give the gold to them, and give some in charity.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1826.commentary: The incident highlights that there was a time when such honesty and integrity prevailed amongst men that buyers and sellers were more concerned with practicing upon religious teachings than lining their pockets. Scholars state that this incident transpired during the reign of Dāwūd (عليه السلام) who reconciled between the two parties in an amazingly wise manner.

1827.text: He heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "There were once two women and each of them had her child with her. A wolf came and took away the child of one of them. She said to her companion: 'The wolf took away your child.' The other said: 'No, it took away your child.' They took their dispute to Dā'ūd (عليه السلام) and he ruled in favour of the elder woman. They then went to Sulaymān ibn Dā'ūd (عليه السلام) and informed him. He said: 'Bring me a knife so that I may divide the child between the two of you.' The younger woman said: 'Do not do that, may Allāh be merciful to you. It is her child.' So he ruled in favour of the younger woman." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1827.commentary: Sulaymān (عليه السلام) here used a ḥīlā (legal stratagem) to ascertain the mother of the child because he knew that a true mother would never permit her child to be killed. This proves the permissibility of using a ḥīlā to establish the truth or to benefit Islām. Ḥīlā's for purposes that harm Islām are a grave sin and not at all permissible.

1828.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The righteous people will pass away one after another until only the scum will remain like the residue of barley or dates. They will have no value in the sight of Allāh." (Bukhārī)
1828.commentary: The ḥadīth explains that morality and spirituality will decrease to such an extent at the end of time that no righteous people will remain. At that time, open sinners and people of evil repute will dominate and assume leadership positions. Just as residue has no value, these sinners will have no value in Allāh's (ﷻ) sight. One should cling to the people of knowledge and virtue because they are beloved to Allāh (ﷻ). One should not oppose them for fear of being deprived of Allāh's (ﷻ) mercy. The death of the righteous heralds the approach of Qiyāmah.

1829.narrator: Rifā'ah ibn Rāfi' al-Zuraqī (رضي الله عنه)
1829.text: Jibra'īl came to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and asked: "What honour do those who participated in the battle of Badr have among you?" He replied: "They are among the best of Muslims," or words to that effect. Jibra'īl said: "It is the same with the angels who participated in the battle of Badr." (Bukhārī, Ibn Mājah)
1829.commentary: Muslims fought the battle of Badr against the enemy on the basis of faith and hope in Allāh (ﷻ). They were very few in number and possessed very little weapons. Hence, they were honoured and enjoy great status in Islām.

1830.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When Allāh (ﷻ) sends punishment on a nation, the punishment afflicts all of them. Thereafter, they are raised according to their actions." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1830.commentary: Divine punishments in the form of earthquakes, floods, tornadoes, fires and so forth afflict all people: believers, disbelievers, righteous and sinners. However, on the day of Qiyāmah they will be raised and judged according to their actions. The righteous will be in Paradise and the disobedient will be in Hell-fire. The ḥadīth indicates that one should not befriend and associate excessively with the sinners. One should not remain silent in the face of sin, oppression and injustice.

1831.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to lean on a tree trunk while delivering his sermon. When the pulpit was put in place, we heard the tree trunk crying like a pregnant camel until the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) got down and placed his hand on it. It then became quiet." Another narration has: "When it was the day of Jumu'ah, the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) sat on the pulpit. The tree trunk from which he used to deliver the sermon cried out until it almost burst open." Another narration has: "It cried like a child. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) got down and embraced it. It began to sob like a child that is made to keep quiet and it finally became silent. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'It cried because of the remembrance of Allāh which it used to hear.'" (Bukhārī)
1831.commentary: This ḥadīth narrates a miracle of the Messenger (ﷺ), namely the crying of a tree trunk due to his separation. When Ḥasan Baṣrī (رحمه الله) used to narrate this ḥadīth he would instinctively burst into tears and remark, 'When a dry piece of wood cried on account of his love, you should cry to a greater extent in his love and in expectation of meeting him.'

1832.narrator: Abū Tha'labah al-Khushanī Jurthūm ibn Nāshir (رضي الله عنه)
1832.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) made certain things obligatory, so do not neglect them. He laid down certain limits, so do not exceed them. He prohibited certain things, so do not indulge in them. He was silent about certain things as a mercy to you and not because of forgetfulness, so do not delve into them." (Dāraquṭnī, Ḥākim, Bayhaqī)
1832.commentary: Imām Sam'ānī (رحمه الله) stated that this ḥadīth occupies a pivotal role in Islām and that one who abides by its instructions will attain ultimate success. "Obligatory" things refer to matters which Islām regards as compulsory such as ṣalāh, fasting, zakāh, Ḥaj, etc. "Limits" refer to those matters which Islām has laid down penal punishments for such as adultery, theft, slander, etc.

1833.narrator: Abdullāh ibn Abī Aufā (رضي الله عنه)
1833.text: We went with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on seven expeditions during which we ate locusts." Another narration has: "We ate locusts with him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasa'ī)
1833.commentary: Consuming locusts is permissible according to all the four Imāms. It is not established that the Messenger (ﷺ) ever ate locusts, however he did not prevent the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) from doing so.

1834.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A believer is not bitten from the same hole twice." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1834.commentary: During the era of the Messenger (ﷺ), there was a poet by the name of Abū Ghazzah. He would recite poetry inciting the enemies against Islām. He was captured during the battle of Badr and brought before the Messenger (ﷺ). He apologised for his wrongs and the Messenger (ﷺ) took an oath from him that he would not return to his old ways. However, he broke his oath and again began composing evil poetry. When he was captured during the battle of Uḥud, he again promised never to compose such poetry, but the Messenger (ﷺ) had him killed. When people questioned the Messenger (ﷺ) about this, he mentioned that a believer is not bitten from the same hole twice.
